places.name: The Held Breath
sources: module 20 §12.3b hard-to-reach types (underwater grottoes, air pockets, flooded cellars)
uesp:Lore:Argonian (amphibious physiology; the crossing is priced around held breath)

why.founding: The Held Breath is a maintained air pocket on a flooded root route. Divers keep the pocket in repair so that the crossing is survivable.
why.siteAdvantages: The pocket lies at the midpoint of the longest flooded branch in the region.
why.occupantsMotive: The pocket is unstaffed. Passers-by maintain it under an interior custom. Anyone who uses the shelter repairs it before leaving.
why.pressures: The seal leaks. The pocket is smaller each decade. The Waykeepers who could reseal it will not work outside a paid line.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the pocket were lost, the flooded route would become impassable. Every crossing would then go by the long root gallery. That route takes a day longer and is a band of danger worse.

preferences: water relation: fully enclosed by water
neighbours: inside a drowned or flooded place

places.traversalFallback: The fallback is to walk the surface route. The walk takes two days over D5 ground.

vibe.silhouette: The pocket shows nothing from outside. Divers find it by diving.
vibe.palette: The root-brown walls are lit by a single carried lamp. Silver bubbles pin under the ceiling. The tally scars are pale against the dark bark. A dropped flower has gone black at the dive line.
vibe.materials: The seal is old resin that was poured thin and is cracking at the rim. The bubble ceiling is bare root with no lashing at all. The tally marks are cut, not painted. There are four hundred of them. The dry stores are wedged into a natural root shelf.
vibe.signatureFeature: A dry bubble the size of a room lies thirty metres down a flooded gallery. A tally is cut into the root, with one mark for each rest taken.
vibe.condition: The seal is thinner every year. The Waykeepers have not been paid to reseal it.
vibe.approach: The dive to the pocket is one held breath from the last air.
vibe.senses: Divers hold their breath. They hear the pop of a fresh air pocket breaking the surface. Cold water presses at the ankles even when the chest is dry. The ceiling drips on a slow count. Divers use the count to time the next dive.

playerPurpose.hook: A room of dry air lies thirty metres down a flooded root gallery. Four hundred marks in the wall record one rest each.

loot.provenance: left for the next traveller, by shelter custom

places.name: Alten Markmont
sources: Lore:Alten Markmont (Arena gazetteer); Lore:East Empire Company

why.founding: Alten Markmont is a trading station that faces outsiders. It was built where the southern water route met the Helstrom approach. The alten- prefix marks it as never Argonian.
why.siteAdvantages: The station has a landing on deep-enough water. It lies at the last point at which outsiders were tolerated.
why.occupantsMotive: A skeleton staff of two factors runs the station. Those who shelter in the warehouses also stay there. A company that no longer trades here pays the two factors a retainer. The company holds that a lapsed post is cheaper to hold than to re-license.
why.pressures: The interior tolerates the station but does not need it. The trade that the station was built for stopped. The warehouses now shelter people whom the factors are not allowed to register.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single busy season would refill the station. The Helstrom assembly has decided that there will not be one.

preferences: water relation: on a navigable route inland
neighbours: too far inland for its own logistics

vibe.silhouette: A company mark hangs on the wall of a building that is far too large for its occupancy.
vibe.palette: The quay stone is weathered grey. Faded company red shows on peeling paint. Brown floodwater laps the loading step. Dust lies pale on the empty shelving.
vibe.materials: An Imperial company crew raised the dressed stone quay walls. The warehouse timber is squared and jointed, with no local lashing. The roof shingle was imported once and has never been matched since. Iron strapping is rusting loose at the hinges.
vibe.signatureFeature: Imperial warehouse frontage stands over a quay that the marsh has taken back to the knee. The frontage was never blended with a single Argonian building.
vibe.condition: Two factors keep the ledgers. The roof goes unrepaired.
vibe.mood: The station is commercial architecture without a trade. Dry rot affects the roof beams.
vibe.approach: The stone shows through the reeds a long way before the buildings resolve.
vibe.senses: Damp paper and old ledger dust hang in the warehouse air. Standing water slaps at the loading step. Canvas awnings hang slack in still air. A bell hangs unrung between convoys.

questHooks.opportunity: Three parties hold paper on stock that has not moved for a century. A quest can decide whose paper the marsh honours.

places.whySiteWon: summit in firm lowland (danger band 4), 696 m from the nearest route; won on nearPoint, culture-clump, region.

playerPurpose.hook: An Imperial warehouse quarter has been taken back to the knee by the marsh. The stock still sits on the racks. The stock has gone unclaimed since the Imperial factor stopped coming.

loot.provenance: what a village keeps for guests it half-trusts

places.sitingNote: The site is bound to the southern channel that its founding names. An outsiders' landing has to be on navigable water. The unconstrained plot left the site 260 m dry of the nearest channel.

places.name: Thousand-Chimes
sources: Lore:Bright-Throat Village; Lore:Argonian (jewellery, guarded weaving secrets)

why.founding: Thousand-Chimes is a craft village that makes bone and tin chimes. Half the province listens to its Hist through those chimes.
why.siteAdvantages: The village stands beside a hero Hist whose wind is reliable. The makers tune each chime against the tree that will hang it.
why.occupantsMotive: The chime-makers hold a tuning that is a religious qualification, not a trade skill. The tree-minders examine and license the tuning. A maker who loses the qualification loses the craft and the village at once.
why.pressures: Cheap cast chimes from the cities undercut the makers. The makers say that the cast chimes mistranslate the trees. The tree-minders have declined to rule on that for six years.
why.wouldChangeIf: A ruling that cast chimes are valid would end the village's authority. The coastal foundries would then take the province's trade within a decade.

preferences: water relation: within poling reach of a trade channel, though the tuning tree sets the site
neighbours: on a trade water; brokers between neighbours

vibe.silhouette: Chimes, clacking looms and forge smoke announce the village before it comes into view.
vibe.palette: The chime metal is brass and bone. Forge-smoke grey lies against the green canopy. Resin catches gold in the tuning bowls. Dye batches stain the bark.
vibe.materials: Chime frames are racked by pitch in the tuning shed. The forge roofs are shingled and are patched where sparks have caught. The benches are worn pale at the grip from years of filing. The licensing tree is strung with sample chimes at every reachable branch.
vibe.signatureFeature: A tuning field holds two hundred hung frames. The makers walk through the field in silence to test a batch.
vibe.condition: The village is kept exact under the tree-minders' licence. Nothing is left loose.
vibe.approach: The sound carries a kilometre. At closer range, the sound resolves into a village.
vibe.senses: Hammer taps on tin sound between long silences. Hot metal and cut sap smell in the same breath. The tuning field rings as a batch is walked past. Bone dust grits underfoot near the workbenches.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can pull a tuning qualification, restore one or prove a chime false.

playerPurpose.hook: Two hundred hung frames stand in a field. The makers will tune a chime to a named tree, if they are given the name.

places.name: The Under-Ring

why.founding: The Barsaebic Ayleid works predate the works of the interior tribes. The Barsaebic Ayleid works go down into the ground and do not rise above it.
why.siteAdvantages: The Ayleids built rings underground. The rings fill from beneath every wet season. The rings drain again afterwards.
why.occupantsMotive: No speaking creature lives in the Under-Ring. The lower rings are dry. Animals den in the lower rings.
why.pressures: Antiquarians want to enter the Under-Ring. The interior tribes have no stake either way. Two licensed parties went down. Neither licensed party came back up.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dig licence from any authority would open the Under-Ring. The Helstrom assembly would then decide whether Ayleid stone falls under the Duskfall taboo.

preferences: water relation: dry, elevated
neighbours: in the north and west, where the Barsaebic Ayleids went

vibe.silhouette: White stone arches and columns stand here. White is otherwise absent from the colours of the province.
vibe.palette: White stone rings sink into black flood water. Pale lichen crusts the risers. Lamplight shows sharply against the dark stone. No green grows below the first ring.
vibe.materials: The walls are dressed white stone laid in courses that no local hand cut. The welkynd settings were picked clean of their stones long ago. The floor drainage channels were cut by a different people than the builders of the walls. Roots have found every seam and split it wider.
vibe.signatureFeature: Ayleid stonework stands here. Argonian root grows through the welkynd settings.
vibe.condition: No living hand maintains the Under-Ring. The rings drain and refill on their own.
vibe.mood: The Under-Ring feels alien. No interior tribe claims an ancestor in it.
vibe.approach: A ring of white stone teeth shows above the mud.
vibe.senses: Cold stone air rises out of the stair. Standing water slaps the lower rings on a slow tide. Grave-goods dust catches at the back of the throat. A call down the stair comes back with no echo.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 435 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.

playerPurpose.hook: Ayleid stone has Argonian root growing through its light-settings. The works go down into water and do not rise into the air.

loot.provenance: Barsaebic work below the water table, unpicked

places.name: Long-Stride

why.founding: The keepers bred lizard-steeds on this rise for two generations. A wet season flooded the schooling paddock. The flood let the breeding stock loose.
why.siteAdvantages: The rise is firm and the paddock ground is soft. That ground once suited training. It now suits a wamasu that has denned in the flooded pens.
why.occupantsMotive: A wamasu took over the paddock. The water is good and undisturbed, so the wamasu stays.
why.pressures: Porters once bought steeds here. Porters now route wide around the pens. The loss of this supply has driven up steed prices on every interior road.
why.wouldChangeIf: Killing or driving off the wamasu would leave the pens open for breeding again. No keeper has tried this since the keepers scattered.

preferences: water relation: penned water separated from open channel
neighbours: supplies mounts or protection to a district

notableNpcSlots.role: ka-deelith who broke the animals to the saddle

vibe.silhouette: The pen rails have collapsed. A burrow mouth lies where the schooling paddock used to be.
vibe.palette: The water of the flooded pens is the colour of tea. The drowned rail-wood is grey. One strand of breeding-tag cord is still red.
vibe.materials: The training rails were built for lizard-steeds. The rails are now underwater and a wamasu holds them. The soft mud of the schooling paddock kept its shape under the flood. The posts are snapped at the waterline where the herd broke out.
vibe.signatureFeature: The laid-pole schooling runs are still visible under the water. The runs are now the approach lanes of the wamasu.
vibe.condition: The pens have not been repaired since the flood took them.
vibe.approach: The herd smell is gone from the pens. The paddock mud is still churned.
vibe.senses: A wake moves under still water before the wamasu is seen. The paddock mud smells of old dung gone sweet with rot. The rails creak when the current pushes them.

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 59 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

playerPurpose.hook: The breeding pens once supplied every porter route in the interior. A wamasu now dens in the flooded pens.

loot.provenance: left by the people who lived here

places.name: The Staying Stone
sources: Lore:Wamasu (Haynekhtnamet of Shadowfen received offerings to stop seasonal flooding)

why.founding: The Staying Stone is a shrine where offerings are made to hold back the flood. Four villages maintain the shrine jointly.
why.siteAdvantages: The shrine stands at the pinch point where the flood enters this basin.
why.occupantsMotive: The shrine has no residents. Four villages take turns keeping it. The turn order is older than any current naheesh of the four villages.
why.pressures: The offerings have not held back the floods for three years. The villages blame each other. They blame chiefly the village whose turn fell in the worst year.
why.wouldChangeIf: One more bad year and the villages will abandon the shrine or rebuild it bigger. Either decision breaks the four-village compact. The compact is joint institution of the district.

preferences: water relation: facing the creature's water
neighbours: between a village and a lair

vibe.silhouette: Offerings are heaped facing a body of water or a den. Open water lies behind the offerings.
vibe.palette: The floodwater is brown against green banks. The offerings are pale on dark stone. The tin chime frames catch grey light. Moss climbs the ledges nearest the water.
vibe.materials: Stone ledges are set four abreast, one per village. The roof beams have been gone since the last storm and the frame stands bare. Each village replaces the rope ties only in its own turn. Paint is renewed yearly over the old marks.
vibe.signatureFeature: The shrine has four offering ledges, one per village. The state of each ledge shows whether its village has kept its turn.
vibe.condition: Each village patches the shrine only when its turn falls due.
vibe.approach: A stone stands in the water. Fresh and rotted offerings lie side by side on it.
vibe.senses: Standing water lies underfoot at every tide. The oldest offerings rot. The newest offerings smell sweet. Cold stone chills wet feet. Gulls work the shallows for scraps.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can find out which of the four villages has stopped keeping its turn.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 290 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, region.

playerPurpose.hook: Four villages share the ledges here. The rot on each ledge shows which village has stopped keeping its turn.

loot.provenance: left by whoever came last

places.name: Keeps-the-Egg
sources: Lore:Hist (a settlement without a Hist is always political)

why.founding: The Hist of the tribe was killed in the Imperial century. The tribe recovered the Mnemic Egg. The tribe organised itself around keeping the Egg.
why.siteAdvantages: The tribe did not move. The dead trunk is still the centre of the village. The Egg is kept inside the trunk.
why.occupantsMotive: The tribe keeps a memory. No member of the tribe can currently read the memory.
why.pressures: Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg. One of the three has publicly offered to buy it. If the tribe refused the offer, it would be seen to be hoarding the Egg.
why.wouldChangeIf: The archivists of the main quest could read the Egg. Reading the Egg would resolve or destroy the tribe. Each claimant tribe has decided which outcome it wants.

preferences: water relation: as a hist-village
neighbours: neighbours argue about whether to admit them

notableNpcSlots.role: Naheesh who forbids talk of the clutch

vibe.silhouette: A dead trunk still stands at the centre of the village. The villagers kept the trunk and did not clear it.
vibe.palette: Bone-pale heartwood scaffolding stands against grey bark. The chamber of the Egg is lit orange from inside. Dust lies thick on the log shelf. The iron on the staff of the naheesh is dulled.
vibe.materials: The dead trunk is propped with green-cut props. Sap seeps from the driven ends of the props. The chamber of the Egg is walled with fitted bark tile with no gaps. The scaffold ladders are lashed fresh each season. The ladders are left rough underfoot.
vibe.signatureFeature: The dead trunk stands in the middle of the village. The villagers scaffold and maintain the trunk like a building. The Egg is housed in a chamber cut into the heartwood of the trunk.
vibe.condition: The scaffold has been rebuilt sound. The trunk itself is past saving.
vibe.mood: The villagers keep their grief as a standing duty.
vibe.approach: A grey trunk with a lit doorway in it shows under the canopy. The trunk is visible from the water.
vibe.senses: The trunk creaks on a slow rhythm. Everyone in the village has stopped hearing the creak. Dust off old bark catches in the throat near the chamber door. Low argument carries from the hut of the naheesh on days when a claimant tribe visits.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can open the reliquary. A quest can arbitrate the three claims. A quest can read what is inside the Egg.
questHooks.tierOwnership: LH29 · tier-3; LH30 · tier-3; LH31 · tier-3

localStateVariants.whatChanges: The chamber is kept dark. The village is closed to visitors.

localStateVariants.when: This state applies after the severance is proved.
localStateVariants.whatChanges: The chamber is opened. The log is made available.

playerPurpose.hook: The village is built around a dead trunk that the villagers refuse to leave. The villagers keep a Mnemic Egg. Three other tribes have claimed the Egg.

places.name: The Lit Fen
sources: Lore:Wamasu (luminescent organs); Lore:Guar (Glowgill); module 55 (night is authored world state, so night-only places are legitimate)

why.founding: The Lit Fen is a fen. Its water lights at night from the fall of Hist-flower.
why.siteAdvantages: The fen is still water directly downstream of the grove of a hero Hist.
why.occupantsMotive: The fen is unkept. The villages come once a year. The night is fixed by the Tsoko stones. The villages come in numbers because of what is in the deep channel.
why.pressures: The fen lights only while the tree above flowers. This year the light came late and stopped early.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the tree failed, the fen would go out. The district would see the fen go dark weeks before any sign appeared in the grove.

preferences: water relation: still or tidal water, undisturbed
neighbours: known and visited; a destination, not a secret

vibe.silhouette: At night the light itself is the landmark. It is visible from further away than any daytime cue in this province.
vibe.palette: The black canopy water burns red after dark. The banks are grey and unlit by day. The drifted flower petals bleach at the waterline. A paler current runs along the line of the channel.
vibe.materials: The fen has no structure beyond root shelf and silt bank. A single old shrine post is driven at the shallow end. A fallen limb is wedged across the water as a crossing. Bare mud is banked where the last flood pushed it.
vibe.signatureFeature: The water is red-lit under a black canopy after dark. The light is brighter or dimmer with the flowering of the tree upstream.
vibe.condition: The fen is unkept between visits. The villages tend it once a year on the fixed night.
vibe.mood: The fen is beautiful. The deep channel is not safe.
vibe.approach: The ground glows beyond a root bank.
vibe.senses: Heat lasts long after sundown. Petals rot sweet at the waterline. The surface flickers when something shifts beneath it. For long stretches the main sound is dripping root.

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.

playerPurpose.hook: After dark the water burns red under a black canopy. The light shows the shape moving under the water.

loot.provenance: the effects of one household, gathered over a lifetime

places.name: The Raw Hold
sources: Lore:Blackrose Prison (the Blackguards' heirs, prison-descended three generations)

why.founding: A Blackguard crew hides in the interior. The crew is found at this place and at no other.
why.siteAdvantages: The Raw Hold lies deep in the interior and off every route. It has a single boat exit.
why.occupantsMotive: The crew are criminals who keep no ledger and have no discipline. Most of them are three generations out of Blackrose. They cannot work in any place where their descent is known.
why.pressures: The crew cannot resupply. They are starting to raid the villages on which they depend. Raiding a village that supplies a crew has ended other crews in the same way.
why.wouldChangeIf: A retaliation by the villages would finish the crew. The interior tribes have already agreed among themselves which village would lead it.

preferences: water relation: boat access, concealed
neighbours: answers to a reoccupied prison

vibe.silhouette: The camp is well built and has a guarded approach. The camp shows no smoke.
vibe.palette: The hull-black timber shows green stain. Rust bleeds down the old iron. Brown water lies at the keel line. No lamp is lit past the second rib.
vibe.materials: The ribs of a beached barge are re-roofed in cut frond. The deck planks were pulled from the hold below and reused. The salvaged nails are driven crooked. A single gangplank is rigged to lift on a signal.
vibe.signatureFeature: The camp is built inside the ribs of a beached river barge. The crew dragged the barge up a creek and never dragged it back.
vibe.condition: The crew patch the camp irregularly. They repair nothing properly.
vibe.approach: A boat hull sits well above the waterline, up a creek.
vibe.senses: The hull creaks as the tide turns. Oil and old fish smell rises from the bilge. Talk is cut short when an unfamiliar boat is heard. Cold iron is under the hand at every rail.

places.whySiteWon: island in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 35 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

playerPurpose.hook: A Blackguard crew lives in the ribs of a barge. The crew could not drag the barge back to the water. The crew have one boat and no friends.

loot.provenance: a crew that cannot spend what it takes

places.name: Many-Ways
sources: Lore:Murkmire (platforms ascending from ground to hover above water)

why.founding: Many-Ways is a village that grew as a junction of walkways. It did not grow around a centre.
why.siteAdvantages: Four routes over soft ground have to meet here. No other place suits them. The junction is the whole capital of the village.
why.occupantsMotive: Walkway-keepers live here. The keepers charge for maintenance. They argue about who owes what.
why.pressures: The walkways cost more to keep than the village earns. The keepers have begun charging tolls. The tribes on the arms consider the tolls extortion.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing one arm of the junction would strand the route of a whole tribe. That tribe has started surveying its own alternative. The tribe would sooner build the alternative than keep paying.

preferences: water relation: crosses water rather than sitting beside it
neighbours: often the only dry route through its stretch

vibe.silhouette: The line of the walkway curves away into the vegetation.
vibe.palette: Reed-green water throws light up under the decking. The cane-pale boards are worn dark at the crossing. Red paint is fresh only on the newest post. Brown mud shows at low tide.
vibe.materials: The decking runs out in four directions from one central span. The keepers replace the cane lashings arm by arm as they can afford it. The shrine hangs on ropes under the crossing. The shrine is a separate structure from the crossing. A toll box is bolted to each of the four approaches.
vibe.signatureFeature: The village has no square. Its centre is a five-way walkway junction. A shrine hangs under the deck where the routes cross.
vibe.condition: The keepers maintain the walkways arm by arm. They maintain the arm of whichever tribe has paid that season.
vibe.approach: Decking can be seen among the reeds. The village begins at the first boards.
vibe.senses: The boards drum underfoot where four lines of traffic cross. Fish and cut cane scent the air. Poles knock against the pilings at the mooring. Voices are raised over the toll boxes most evenings.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can audit the repair ledger of the keepers. A quest can cost the junction an arm.
questHooks.tierOwnership: LH32 · tier-3; LH33 · tier-3; LH34 · tier-3

playerPurpose.hook: Four walkway routes have to meet somewhere. The shrine hung under the deck where they cross is the nearest thing to a town square.

places.name: The Pulled Field
sources: docs/quests/20-world-provisions.md §12b (grave-stakes; pulling one raises a bog blight)
Lore:Argonian (pulling a grave-stake raises a bog blight); fauna-hazards dossier (pahnjees)

why.founding: The Pulled Field is a grave-pole field. Looters pulled the poles from the ground. The poles had been holding something down. That something has now risen.
why.siteAdvantages: The field is the burial ground of an old village. No living village stands near it now.
why.occupantsMotive: Bog blights live in the field. The grave-singers send their apprentices here to train. They do this without announcing it.
why.pressures: Looters still pull the poles because the goods buried under them are real. The looters are the heirs of the village that abandoned the field.
why.wouldChangeIf: Restaking the field would settle the matter. It would also settle the question of who owns the grave goods. No local family has offered to pay for the work.

preferences: water relation: soft ground, flood-disturbed
neighbours: at or beside a grave-stake field

vibe.silhouette: Driven poles fill the field. One pole is down. A pahnjee rack has been left to sag.
vibe.palette: The grave-poles are pale against the black mud. Cord bands on them still hold their paint. The empty holes are darker than the ground around them.
vibe.materials: The original binders drove the poles straight and deep. Looters' rope marks scar every pulled post. The holes are undisturbed below the pull line.
vibe.signatureFeature: Pulled poles lie beside their own holes. Each pole is still wrapped in knotted cord and paint bands. The bands name the person who lies under the pole.
vibe.condition: Looters pull poles faster than any family replaces them.
vibe.mood: The burial ground is no longer holding.
vibe.approach: Holes lie in rows across a field.
vibe.senses: The ground gives underfoot where a pole used to anchor it. Wet cord and old paint smell faintly of tallow. Loose poles rattle as they knock together in the wind.

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 4), 330 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

playerPurpose.hook: Looters pulled the grave-poles. What the poles held down has risen. The cord and paint still name each grave.

loot.provenance: what the looters had already lifted and dropped

places.name: The Carriers' Rest
sources: Lore:Argonian (bones brought to the dirt redeem a death away from the Hist); White Rose Prison

why.founding: The Carriers' Rest is a staging post on the bone route. Carriers bring the bones of Argonians who died away from the Hist back to the dirt.
why.siteAdvantages: The water route meets the interior walking route here. It is the last point where a bundle can be re-wrapped and re-labelled before the walk. A cold store is cut into the rise under the racks. Unclaimed bundles have been stacked in the store since the office opened.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers live here. Carrying is a recognised and feared profession. The family pays the carriers. The village does not pay them. The carriers' loyalty therefore runs to the dead.
why.pressures: The 4E produced more distant dead than the route can carry.
why.wouldChangeIf: A backlog is already visible in the racks. A second season of backlog would force the carriers to choose which families' dead go first. The families do not want the carriers to hold that power.

preferences: water relation: on a walked or poled route
neighbours: at the junction of the river route and the interior walking route

vibe.silhouette: A rack of wrapped bundles stands under a roof. Each bundle is labelled with a village name.
vibe.palette: Pale wrapped bundles lie under a dark roof. Chalk marks cover the delivery board. Brown river water lies below the cellar door. The racks are grey bark.
vibe.materials: The racks are built to a standard bundle length. They are not built to a person's length. The cellar door is cut straight into the bank and shored with timber. Numbered tags are carved fresh for each arrival. The roof is kept sound because the cargo cannot get wet.
vibe.signatureFeature: Numbered racks hold wrapped bone bundles. The bundles wait for a carrier who is going the right way. A delivery board stands in the yard like the board of a freight office.
vibe.condition: The carriers keep the racks full. The carriers sweep the yard daily.
vibe.approach: The full racks stand at the front of the yard.
vibe.senses: Dry cold rises from the cellar store. Resin seals the wrappings. Rope pulleys creak as they lower a bundle. Talk is kept to names and numbers.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 27 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, route.

vibe.materials: The mudflat is unworked. The families dug drainage channels that cut it. Wreck hulls are half-buried and rotted through on the sun side only. Dropped cargo is scattered, with wood swollen and metal seized. No shelter is built here because the season is too short.
vibe.signatureFeature: In the dry weeks the flat is a floor of exposed wrecks, dropped cargo and older things. The families argue every year over who may take what.
vibe.condition: The families pick the flat over each year while the window is open.
vibe.approach: The flat is a lake one month and a field of objects the next.
vibe.senses: Mud cracks underfoot with a sound like breaking crockery. Drying silt smells sharp and mineral. Heat comes off the exposed flat. No shade stands anywhere on it.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 240 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

places.name: The Sap Wallow
sources: Lore:Bright-Throat; Lore:Naga-Kur (starblossom, red paint, the kaju kill)

why.founding: The Sap Wallow is a natural sap pool that is used for sanctioned communion. The nearest tree-minder licenses its use.
why.siteAdvantages: A hero Hist's roots surface in a hollow and fill it.
why.occupantsMotive: A tender controls dose and turn. The tree-minder appoints the tender. The tender answers to the grove and not to the users.
why.pressures: Unlicensed users come at night. The tender knows and mostly allows it. The tender calculates that a policed wallow becomes a starblossom hollow.
why.wouldChangeIf: Overuse would produce another Miredance. Miredance is two days away. The tender cites it against the users who want the dose raised.

preferences: water relation: a mud wallow
neighbours: a short walk from a village, out of its sight

vibe.silhouette: A fenced amber pool has a single shelter over its deep end. No path leads away from the pool.
vibe.palette: The amber-warm pool is ringed in green shade. Pale stone dose-cups sit on their ledge. Red flower heads drift at the rim. Steam ribbons up where the water runs hottest.
vibe.materials: The sap-fed pool is banked in shaped root. The tribe adds one graft each generation. A cane fence marks the licensed edge. A single frond shelter roofs the deep end. Worn stone steps lead down into the warmth.
vibe.signatureFeature: The water is warm amber at blood heat. A queue of stone dose-cups sits on a ledge, sized from a thimble to a bowl. The tender sets which cup a bather is given.
vibe.condition: The tender watches the pool day and night. The tender patches it by hand each season.
vibe.approach: The heat carries first. The smell follows.
vibe.senses: Sweet resin thickens the air near the surface. Blood-warm water laps at bare skin. The tender's low counting voice marks doses. Distant chimes sound the licensed hour.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 297 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.umpholo-mission (+0.66).

playerPurpose.hook: The pool is sap-warm water at blood heat. A row of dose cups runs from a thimble to a bowl. The tender decides which cup a bather is given.

loot.provenance: left by whoever came last

places.name: Starblossom Hollow
sources: Lore:Bright-Throat; Lore:Naga-Kur (starblossom, red paint, the kaju kill)

why.founding: Starblossom Hollow is a wallow that is used for the other kind of dreaming. The users have received no permission from any tree.
why.siteAdvantages: The hollow is cold. Starblossom grows thickly there.
why.occupantsMotive: The wallow is unlicensed. Users come here. One man from the licensed wallow sells to them. He is not supposed to be here at all.
why.pressures: The tree-minders regard the hollow as the theft of a rite. Twice they have asked the assembly to name it. Naming it would make it prosecutable.
why.wouldChangeIf: A crackdown would move the hollow. It would not end it. The plant grows in every cold hollow in the district. The hollows have not been counted.

preferences: water relation: a mud wallow
neighbours: a short walk from a village, out of its sight

vibe.silhouette: "After dark the hollow is lit blue-white. The flowers grow nowhere else throughout the region."
vibe.palette: Blue-white starblossom stands against black water. The green canopy fades to grey at the rim. The root-wood is bleached pale where feet cross it. One lamp is kept low for the sleepers.
vibe.materials: Raised beds are cut into the hollow floor and are edged with root. Sleeping mats are staked to low platforms. A watcher's lean-to is roofed in frond. Collecting bowls are set under the flower stems.
vibe.signatureFeature: Starblossom is farmed here in careful beds. The farmers insist that they are not farmers. The beds are laid out as a constellation.
vibe.condition: The farmers run the hollow carefully. The beds are laid out as a constellation.
vibe.approach: Blue-white flowering stands in a [view/scene] that is otherwise red-flowered.
vibe.senses: The sweetness is thick enough to taste at the back of the throat. The sleepers breathe slowly on the mats. Cold settles over the water after dark. A single bell is struck when a sleeper wakes wrong.

playerPurpose.hook: Starblossom is farmed in constellation beds by people who insist that they are not farmers. They sell to visitors. They watch any visitor who looks at the beds too long.

loot.provenance: left by whoever came last

places.name: The Pull
sources: module 50 (tides and water levels as world state); Lore:Sea Transportation

why.founding: The Pull is a narrows. The wet-season flow becomes lethal there for a fortnight.
why.siteAdvantages: The narrows is the crossing on this reach, at the pinch.
why.occupantsMotive: The narrows has no residents. The nearest village posts a watch in season, which is unpaid. The rota falls mostly on the two poorest households.
why.pressures: The watch lapses in some years. It lapses in the years when the village's men work the porter relay.
why.wouldChangeIf: A bridge would solve the danger. Four villages would use a bridge. Each village holds that the crossing benefits the others more, so none of the four has paid for one.

preferences: water relation: the hazard IS the water
neighbours: on a boat lane; forces a portage or a wait

vibe.silhouette: The water's surface is visibly wrong at the pinch.
vibe.palette: Brown current folds over itself at the pinch. The fatal mark on the depth stake is painted stark red. Pale waterlogged drift timber lies along both banks. The water shows no reflection where it moves fastest.
vibe.materials: A stake is driven at the narrows. The villagers recut its paint marks after each drowning. Drift timber and packed silt are banked where the current turns. A swimmer who got clear left a small cairn of stones. The pinch has no built crossing, no rail and no bridge.
vibe.signatureFeature: A depth-and-flow stake has the fatal mark painted on it. The dates of the last four drownings are cut beside the mark.
vibe.condition: The stake resurfaces each year. The crossing is unfixed.
vibe.approach: The stake is visible from both banks. The current reads as slack water until the pinch.
vibe.senses: The pull of the current is audible before it is visible. Still air holds the smell of standing water on either side of the pinch. The water turns suddenly cold at the centre of the channel. The stake creaks against the flow.

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 729 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on culture-clump, region, remote.

playerPurpose.hook: A depth stake has the fatal mark painted on it. The dates of the last four drownings are cut beside it. The nearest village posts a watch through the season.

loot.provenance: The loot was carried in by a traveller who never left.

places.name: The Unmade Work
sources: Lore:Duskfall; material-culture (stone as a moral error post-Duskfall) — this type is where that rule is visibly made

why.founding: The Unmade Work is a xanmeer. Its own builders took it apart at the Duskfall. They did not abandon it.
why.siteAdvantages: The builders carried the stone away. What remains is the plan of the building and not the building.
why.occupantsMotive: The site is untended. The heretic-stone village quarries it. The village is condemned for that. The condemnation has not stopped a single cart.
why.pressures: The site is the clearest physical evidence of the renunciation. The restarted work is quarrying it away.
why.wouldChangeIf: Rebuilding on the site would settle the Duskfall argument in public. The Helstrom assembly has avoided visiting for eleven years.

hardConstraints: remote: at least a kilometre from Alten Corimont, far from the start water and its landings
preferences: water relation: raised
neighbours: in xanmeer country; contrasts directly with the tended and sealed ones
isolated: nothing that a traveller in their first hours would meet

vibe.silhouette: Dressed stone lies in stacks. A foundation has no building on it.
vibe.palette: The foundation stone is bare and grey. Straight lines are cut into bare earth. No colour marks the place where the walls used to stand.
vibe.materials: A full xanmeer footprint has every block quarried away. Fresh cart ruts are worn into the clearing floor. Root grows loose through joints that once held mortar.
vibe.signatureFeature: A full-size floor plan of a xanmeer is left in the ground. Every block has been removed.
vibe.condition: The heretic-stone village quarries the site away steadily.
vibe.mood: The unmaking was deliberate. The site is tidier than a ruin.
vibe.approach: Flat ground has straight lines in it. No walls stand.
vibe.senses: The flat open ground has no wall to return a sound. Turned earth and quarry dust scent the air. Wind carries further because no walls break it.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can read the full-size floor plan. A quest can also work out what the builders were unmaking.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 469 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, remote, culture-clump.

playerPurpose.hook: A xanmeer was taken apart by its own builders, block by block. It left a full-size floor plan in the ground. It also left a foundation vault, which the builders left full.

loot.provenance: no family has claimed it since

places.name: The Interrupted Flight
sources: uesp:Morrowind:Tarhiel (the Icarian Flight scrolls near Seyda Neen, 3E 427)

why.founding: A man came out of the sky here, at speed. It happened roughly two hundred years after the same thing happened near Seyda Neen.
why.siteAdvantages: The site has no advantage. No road and no village lies within an hour of the ferns where he landed.
why.occupantsMotive: He was not going anywhere near here. The letter in his satchel is addressed to a teacher in the tradition. The letter says that he has read the great experimenter's notes and corrected the error. In the letter he writes that the descent is the easy part.
why.pressures: Scavengers, water and the season threaten the site. The satchel is oiled leather. The scrolls in it still work.
why.wouldChangeIf: A finder takes the scrolls. Whether the letter goes with them decides whether his teacher ever hears.

preferences: The place lies far from any road, lane, track or walkway. It is an obscure corner that has no reason to be crossed.
water relation: dry ground, so the satchel is still there
neighbours: deliberately isolated; no village or camp within earshot

places.traversalFallback: No route leads to the site. Travellers arrive only by being lost.

vibe.silhouette: The site is invisible from more than a few paces off. A break in the ferns has the shape of a man.
vibe.palette: The ferns are broken pale where the body fell. Brown leather has gone dark with damp. Scroll paper greys at the torn edge.
vibe.materials: A robe of fine cloth is split at the seams. A satchel is sealed well enough to keep the scrolls dry. Soft ground took the shape of the fall and kept it. No marker or grave-goods have been added since.
vibe.signatureFeature: A crater a body deep lies in soft ground. A satchel beside it holds his jump scrolls. The scrolls are still usable.
vibe.condition: The site is untouched since the fall. The ferns are slowly closing over it.
vibe.approach: No path leads to the crater. Travellers find it by walking into it.
vibe.senses: Crushed fern gives off a green sap smell. Still air lies undisturbed by any path in or out. Paper rustles dry when wind finds the crater. No birdsong sounds directly over the site.

playerPurpose.hook: A man came out of the sky here and did not survive the landing. The scrolls in his satchel are undamaged.

creatures.provenance: a hackwing flock that has held the body since the week he came down

loot.provenance: his tradition's jump scrolls, in an oiled satchel that kept the water out

places.name: The Fenlord's Reach

why.founding: The Fenlord's Reach is an Ayleid fenlord's tomb. The marsh has kept the ground around it sealed.
why.siteAdvantages: The tomb lies in a deep basin with no route and no neighbours. The marsh has kept the seal wet. The stone has therefore not moved.
why.occupantsMotive: The occupants of the tomb lie undisturbed since before the Duskfall. They are unrelated to what the interior tribes recognise as dead.
why.pressures: The tomb is intact. Two antiquarian parties are known to have entered. The second party went looking for the first.
why.wouldChangeIf: Only a breach of the drainage would change it. The drainage has held for an age.

preferences: water relation: dry, sealed
neighbours: near a Barsaebic compound

vibe.silhouette: A low formal stone entrance is framed by carving. The ground hides the entrance well.
vibe.palette: Black stone is carved in low relief that has gone soft with age. The crocodile skulls on the gate posts are bone-white. Grave goods lie dull gold under standing water. Moss climbs the door frame in one thin green line.
vibe.materials: The dressed Ayleid stone is jointed without mortar. The seams are still tight. The original drainage channel is still cut and running. It is unrepaired because it has never needed repair. Grave goods lie untouched as they were interred. No later hand has added anything.
vibe.signatureFeature: The approach is flooded. The drainage of the tomb still works after an age.
vibe.condition: The tomb was sealed and undisturbed until two antiquarian parties entered. One party did not return.
vibe.mood: The work is Ayleid. It is older than any Argonian claim on this ground.
vibe.approach: Travellers find the tomb from a document and not from the ground.
vibe.senses: Standing water drips on a beat that never varies. Cold stone air carries no trace of the swamp's heat. A low structural groan sounds somewhere in the deeper chambers.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 357 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.

playerPurpose.hook: The marsh has kept an Ayleid tomb sealed since before the Duskfall. Its own drainage still works.

loot.provenance: an Ayleid fenlord's grave goods, laid out and undisturbed

why.founding: Six households live on ground that stays dry for two kilometres round in the wet season.
why.siteAdvantages: One-Rise is a single flood-high rise. The households occupy all of it.
why.occupantsMotive: Farmers live here who cannot expand and will not leave. They work back-swamp rice. The rice exists only because the rise splits the flood.
why.pressures: Every neighbour wants shelter on the rise in the wet season. The households cannot house them. The neighbours remember the refusals longer than the floods.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wetter decade would make the rise a refuge camp and not a hamlet. The households already know which of them would have to go.

preferences: water relation: above the seasonal maximum, beside a channel
neighbours: refuge for its neighbours in flood
water relation: the rise stands in water for part of the year

vibe.silhouette: Structures stand on the high ground. They stand alone in a flat view.
vibe.palette: Green lies over standing brown water. The root-wood has gone silver with wet. Sap-gold runs in one bright line. Red flowers grow on the high ground. None grow below the flood mark.
vibe.materials: A shell of trained root stands here. Its floor is a single flattened buttress. The builders used hardwood pegs and withy, with no metal. The structure is unroofed since the last blow and is not yet re-shingled. Totems of wood, mud and plumage stand at the approach.
vibe.signatureFeature: The rise is fully built to its edge. The wet-season waterline is painted on every wall at chest height.
vibe.condition: The households maintain the hamlet just enough and no more.
vibe.mood: The hamlet is cramped and self-sufficient. It is unwelcoming in wet months.
vibe.approach: In the wet season the rise is an island. The village is as large as the island.
vibe.senses: The boards spring underfoot at every step. Chimes rattle on a frame set above the flood mark. Wet bark and cut root smell like a woodyard in rain. No birds sound within earshot.

playerPurpose.hook: Six households live on the last dry ground for two kilometres. The wet-season waterline is painted on every wall at chest height.

loot.provenance: what a village keeps for guests it half-trusts

places.name: Greenspring

why.founding: Greenspring was founded beside the Panther Race. The founders chose springs whose water can be drunk unboiled. Unboiled drinking water is rare in this region. The tribe's Hist grows over the spring.
why.siteAdvantages: Greenspring stands on firm ground. Clean water rises from the spring. A lip of boulders rings the spring. The spring is a short walk from the road. The spring is a short walk from the river landing.
why.occupantsMotive: The tribe serves travellers bound for Helstrom. The tribe has made itself indispensable to those travellers. The tribe charges nothing for water. The tribe charges a great deal for beds and rope.
why.pressures: Salt is reaching the spring water from upstream. The Hist has begun to sicken. The village blames the salt works for the salt in the water. Traffic for Helstrom brings cult couriers, tappers and the Veiled Reed's factors. The tribe does not wish to host those visitors.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the spring soured, the village would have to move to find fresh water. Travellers bound for Helstrom would then lose their surest clean water.

hardConstraints: On the fork below The Panther Race.
preferences: water relation: spring head on a channel bank, always with a landing
neighbours: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage

vibe.silhouette: A sick crown leans over the spring. Huts stand round the spring.
vibe.palette: A pool of clear water lies under the Hist. The green crown of the Hist thins to open sky above. Painted urns stand along the yards. Brown churned mud lies at the landing.
vibe.materials: A tent stands beside the spring. The village has mud-walled pods and huts on mud pads. Beached canoes and a plank boat lie on the bank at the landing. The landing has no plank stage.
vibe.signatureFeature: Visitors drink water from the clear pool under the Hist without ceremony. Visitors are expected to taste the water before they speak.
vibe.condition: The yards that are used daily are well kept. The ground that lies a step off the path is threadbare.
vibe.approach: On the way up from the landing, black river water gives way to a small clear pool under the Hist. Frond smoke from the cookfires reaches the landing before the houses are in sight.
vibe.senses: Visitors taste cold mineral water before a word is spoken. The landing smells of wet rope and boat tar. Voices barter over bed and rope prices. Frond smoke drifts from the cookfires at dusk.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can settle the spring's use in writing. A quest can also foul the spring.

places.name: The Far Shelter
sources: Lore:Black Marsh (guides choose when to move and refuse to stop where you want)

why.founding: The Far Shelter is the second night's shelter on the basin crossing. The guides keep the shelter stocked themselves.
why.siteAdvantages: The shelter stands on defensible dry ground, an islet in deep marsh. The ground lies at the right distance along the crossing.
why.occupantsMotive: Travellers crossing the basin use the shelter. A caretaker stays there in season. The guides pay the caretaker by a joint levy. The guides have not collected the levy in full since they agreed it.
why.pressures: Travellers take stores from the shelter and do not replace them. The guides have started marking the crates. The marks show whose clients took the stores.
why.wouldChangeIf: An unstocked shelter costs lives. The guides at the gate camp price the second night higher than the first. They price it higher because of the risk of an unstocked shelter.

preferences: water relation: defensible, on a channel
neighbours: on a guided route, day-travel spacing
on the first day's march of the basin crossing from the Helstrom gate, not deep in the D5 field — MQ27's shelters must read as a chain

notableNpcSlots.role: Guide who decides when the party moves

vibe.silhouette: The shelter is hard-roofed and stands on the last dry ground. A bell frame and a distance board stand beside it.
vibe.palette: Pale palisade timber stands against dark canopy. Ink on the ledger board is black on grey wood. Embers glow red in the banked fire pit. The chalked distance marker has gone white.
vibe.materials: The palisade is made of driven stakes lashed twice over. A bell frame stands beside the gate. A ledger post carries the season's tally sheets, which are nailed up. Sleeping shelves run along the inner wall.
vibe.signatureFeature: A stock ledger records every taking with a signature. Unsigned takings are listed separately. Each unsigned taking is listed with a description of the taker.
vibe.condition: The guides restocked the shelter hard this year. The shelter had two seasons of shortfall before this year.
vibe.mood: The mood is relieved and short of stores.
vibe.approach: A palisade ring encloses a fire pit. The shelter stands on the first rise since the gate.
vibe.senses: Fire smoke hangs under the palisade roofline. Stakes settle and creak through the night. Parties compare crossings in low voices. Bedding is still damp come morning.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can audit the stores. A quest can arrive to find the stores gone.

places.whySiteWon: islet in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 411 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, landform.

playerPurpose.hook: The Far Shelter is the second night's shelter on the basin crossing. The guides stock it themselves. A ledger records who took what and who did not sign.

places.name: Gate-Side Camp
sources: Lore:Black Marsh (guides choose when to move and refuse to stop where you want)

why.founding: Basin guides wait for hire at this camp outside the Helstrom gate.
why.siteAdvantages: The camp stands just outside the gate, 50 m west of the west basin gate. Inside the gate is the city's own ground. Guides loitering inside the gate are not welcome in the city.
why.occupantsMotive: The guides price by the day and by the route. A guide will refuse a route outright and will not negotiate it.
why.pressures: Guides die in the basin. The camp's roster is shorter than it was. The basin has not got worse. Traffic has got heavier and less experienced.
why.wouldChangeIf: The deep-basin expedition needs a hiring on a large scale. That hiring would empty the camp of its competent guides for a season.

preferences: water relation: defensible, on a channel
neighbours: on a guided route, day-travel spacing

notableNpcSlots.role: Senior guide who decides when the party moves

vibe.silhouette: The hiring camp stands close against the Helstrom gate line. The camp is all frontage and has no depth.
vibe.palette: Cook-fire orange stands against Helstrom's grey wall. Route-board ink is faded where hands touch it most. Root-brown mud is packed hard by traffic. Red appears on the newest guide's tally mark and nowhere else.
vibe.materials: Tents are pitched hard against the gate ditch. The camp allows no permanent structure. A hire board is nailed up and repainted route by route. Cook fires are ringed in cut stone taken from the road verge. Bedding rolls are stacked ready for guides between hires.
vibe.signatureFeature: A hire board lists routes with a price and a survival rate beside each. The survival rates are honest. A guide caught softening a rate loses the board.
vibe.condition: The guides rebuild the camp each season. Nothing in the camp is meant to last.
vibe.approach: Fires burn immediately outside a city that has no suburbs.
vibe.senses: Woodsmoke lies thick over the camp at dusk. Low bargaining voices run through the evening. The causeway's hum carries up from the gate. Boots and packs lie piled wet from the last route back.

questHooks.opportunity: MQ27 expedition guide hire

places.whySiteWon: dry ground 50 m west of Helstrom's basin gate, 5 m above the marsh, outside every district of the city; sited there because the camp's name and its quest text place it at that gate.

places.name: The Roost

why.founding: The Roost is a dead standing grove. Hackwings have used the grove for generations.
why.siteAdvantages: The grove is dead timber with clear flight lines. A roost needs clear flight lines.
why.occupantsMotive: A flock of hackwings lives in the grove. The flock has used the grove for so long that the beast-keepers' grandparents complained about the same birds.
why.pressures: The hackwings take from the beast-keepers' young stock. The beast-keepers want the hackwings gone. The tribe that owns the grove takes hackwing feathers for its rites. That tribe refuses a cull.
why.wouldChangeIf: Culling the roost would end a real nuisance. A cull would cost the owning tribe its feather source. The tribe recognises that feather source as legitimate.

preferences: water relation: none
neighbours: downwind of a lair, a battlefield or a midden

vibe.silhouette: The circling birds mark the roost. They are visible from two ridges off.
vibe.palette: Dead grey timber stands against green canopy. Droppings whiten every branch. Black wings turn overhead.
vibe.materials: The grove is a standing dead grove that no builder has touched. The birds snapped the flight-line branches clean themselves. The roost has no repair of any kind.
vibe.signatureFeature: Two hundred birds leave at first light in one movement. The departure is visible from four kilometres away.
vibe.condition: The grove is left to the birds. No cull has ever stuck.
vibe.approach: The dead grove is grey against green from a long way off.

places.name: High-Flower, the Sarpa Hist

why.occupantsMotive: The winged Sarpa consider the ground a burial place. Their trade, their courts and their hatching all happen above the ground.
why.pressures: The climb is the approach. The tribe has twice refused to cut a stair for the tree-minders' benefit.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the crown platforms in a storm would suspend the rite for a generation. The timber to rebuild them has to come from the hammock village two days away.

places.name: The Kept Line

why.founding: The Kept Line is a tribe that has watched one thing for generations. The watch is now the whole identity of the tribe.
why.siteAdvantages: The village stands on plain ground in shallow marsh, 49 m from a channel. From there the villagers patrol the sealed xanmeer place.hist-heartland.sealed-xanmeer-living. The wardens turn visitors back from the xanmeer.
why.occupantsMotive: The wardens are hereditary. Each warden inherits a post, not a trade. The tribe feeds the wardens in exchange for the watch.
why.pressures: No living warden knows what lies inside the xanmeer that the wardens guard. Each of the last three generations of wardens privately reached a different conclusion.
why.wouldChangeIf: Opening the xanmeer would end the tribe's reason to exist. The wardens fight an antiquarian harder than they fight a looter.

vibe.materials: The gatehouse roof is a bent canopy limb that is rooted at both ends. Every household mends the stockade to one uniform pattern. The stone of the sealed xanmeer behind the fence is left untouched.

places.name: Medusa Wood
sources: fauna-hazards dossier; module 20 §16 (fixed regional danger; D5 stays D5)

why.founding: Medusa Wood is a stand of drowned forest at the edge of the deepest basin water. The tribes give the stand a name in recitation. The tribes do not enter it.
why.siteAdvantages: The wood lies above the deepest standing water in the interior. The drowned forest beneath the wood has not rotted.
why.occupantsMotive: Something lives down there. No two recitations describe it the same way. The recitations name the water. They cite no witness.
why.pressures: The stories are older than the name. The drowned timber is the finest known to the coast dredgers.
why.wouldChangeIf: Little would change the wood. The dredging outfits on the coast have begun asking what it would be worth to lift a stand of unrotted forest.

hardConstraints: remote: at least a kilometre from Alten Corimont, in water where no beginner would be
preferences: water relation: varies by variant
neighbours: the apex hazard of its region; routes bend around it
isolated: nothing that a traveller in their first hours would meet

vibe.silhouette: Grey trunks stand in the water. All of the trunks lean the same way.
vibe.palette: Grey drowned trunks lean uniformly under still black water. Pale light swims through the submerged canopy. Wreck cargo shows dull bronze on the silted floor. Past the treeline the surface shows no colour.
vibe.materials: The standing timber drowned whole and never rotted. The bark is still keyed tight to the wood. Wreck cargo lies among the roots, with the crates burst and spilled. Only the drowned forest stands down here. No built structure stands there. The silt is undisturbed except where a boat has passed.
vibe.signatureFeature: A submerged forest still stands upright. The canopy of the forest lies at swimming depth.
vibe.condition: The wood is unrotted and has stayed unchanged for longer than the tribes have names for it.
vibe.mood: The wood is deep and still. The tribes name it in recitation.
vibe.approach: Seen from a boat, bare grey trunk tips break the surface in a grid. The grid is plainly a forest.
vibe.senses: Underwater the wood is totally quiet, with no current and no fish sound. The cold deepens with each metre of depth. Above the surface, the hull noise of a boat carries too far.

places.name: The Lost City
sources: Lore:Xanmeer (~25% sealed; vakka stones); Lore:Vakka Stone

why.founding: The Lost City was built before the Duskfall around the graft called the Root of Accord. The city was unmade from the map. It was not destroyed.
why.siteAdvantages: The city lies in the deepest ground of the basin. The nearest route is 500.6 m away. The root layer is densest here. The density was grown here.
why.occupantsMotive: The city has no inhabitants. A cult expedition and guardians are present. Whatever the Accord left tending itself has done the same work for an age.
why.pressures: The Unbound Root is trying to reach the city. The Eye is the key.
why.wouldChangeIf: Only the Eye changes the city.

preferences: water relation: raised, often ringed by marsh
neighbours: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it

vibe.silhouette: Terraced massing rises unbroken out of black water. No path leads to it. No path goes round it.
vibe.palette: Black floodwater laps at pale terraced stone. A thin green glow is held only at the sealed entry. Amber lies long dead in the veins of the stone. Colour fades a few steps past the light.
vibe.materials: The city is xanmeer block that was cut and dressed at city scale. No lashed or woven work appears anywhere in it. Root has grown through the stonework and holds old collapses together. A single frontage opens only to the Eye. Silt has sealed every lower course for centuries.
vibe.signatureFeature: A whole terraced city lies under root and water. The forest that grew over the civic streets roofs them.
vibe.condition: The city is sealed. It is not ruined. Contents lie in the places where the Accord set them.
vibe.mood: The city is quiet. It is larger than the Helstrom grove.
vibe.approach: Crossing the basin takes days, with fixed shelters along the way. The frontage then opens only to the Eye.
vibe.senses: Cold rises off ground that ought to hold warmth. An echo returns where the interior swallows sound everywhere else. The standing water tastes of old minerals. A distant working sound comes from guardians that are never seen.

questHooks.opportunity: LOC dungeon.lost_city · BOSS lost_city.last_warden · LOC lost_city.root_sanctuary

places.name: The Wading Ground
sources: Lore:Marsh Giant (killing one is an ecological and religious offence)

why.founding: The Wading Ground is a marsh giant's range. The tribes route around it without discussion.
why.siteAdvantages: The water is deep enough that the giant can stand upright in it. The shallows give the giant feeding ground.
why.occupantsMotive: One giant lives here, with the birds that follow it. The tribes have mapped its hunting pattern closely. They route around it without a guide.
why.pressures: The range of the giant is expanding toward a walkway route. The walkway village has begun asking whether killing a giant is the offence that the tree-minders say it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Moving the walkway costs a season's labour. The tribe that uses the arm least would have to fund the move.

preferences: water relation: wallows and deep marsh
neighbours: a protected territory, mapped by totems

vibe.silhouette: A cleared path runs through vegetation at a wrong height. A totem line stands before the path.
vibe.palette: Clear brown water pales to green above. A wide track flattens red flowers into the mud. Pale bone catches light at head height. Grey churn lines the banks.
vibe.materials: No built structure stands here. The weight of the giant has cut channels through the reed beds. A single depth stick is driven into the bank and left there. A totem line marks the safe route around the giant.
vibe.signatureFeature: The feeding paths of the giant are permanent channels cut through the reed beds. The newest channel points at the walkway.
vibe.condition: The ground is unmanaged. The channels widen a little more each season.
vibe.approach: The channels are readable from the walkway before the giant is in sight.
vibe.senses: The ground trembles faintly before the giant comes into view. Wading birds lift off ahead of it. Reed stems snap out of sight. Standing water goes still again once the giant has passed.

places.name: The Counting Field
sources: Lore:Umbriel; Lore:Knahaten Flu; Lore:Black Marsh (the Great Burn); Lore:Deepmire (the province's Umbriel memorial)

why.founding: The Counting Field is a Knahaten Flu mass grave. It serves the villages that emptied along this reach.
why.siteAdvantages: The ground is flat. It was left unwanted afterwards.
why.occupantsMotive: A memorial keeper from the nearest village tends the field. The post carries no pay. The keeper is exempt from every other village duty.
why.pressures: The count on the stone is disputed. The stone has been recut twice, each time upward. A different tribe paid for each recut.
why.wouldChangeIf: A recount would restart the argument. A recount would also have to include the Kothringi names. The grave-singers have cut no such stake.

preferences: water relation: varies
neighbours: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village

vibe.silhouette: The field is marked ground with no settlement. The field has no burial furniture of the normal kind.
vibe.palette: Pale grey stakes stand in even rows over flat ground. Silt-white water beyond the field catches green light. Charcoal streaks have weathered into three blank stakes. Mud at the low edge of the field is dull brown.
vibe.materials: Driven stakes carry a village name and a cut number. Some of the stakes have been recut twice. Open ground is kept clear of the surrounding root growth. A low wattle fence marks the edge of the field. Nothing is built inside the field. Only the stakes stand here. No shrine structure stands here.
vibe.signatureFeature: There is one stake for every village. There is not one stake for every person. Each stake carries the village name and its final count. Three stakes carry no count at all.
vibe.condition: Stakes are recut when a tribe pays for it. Otherwise the stakes are left as they stand.
vibe.mood: The field feels administrative. The count is disputed.
vibe.approach: Stakes stand at regular intervals. The field looks unlike an ordinary grave field.
vibe.senses: Insects are loud over the open field, where no canopy shades it. Recut names smell of damp stone-dust. Wind carries further here than in the enclosed swamp. The ground is firm and dry underfoot, unlike the land around it.

why.pressures: The trial kills a participant every few years. The last death was an Agaceph boy, in the dry season two years ago. Families whose clutch is not running that year support the trial more readily.
why.wouldChangeIf: A death in the wrong family would force a change. The Agaceph tree-minders have a candidate in the coming season.

neighbours: attached to a village or a pilgrim town

vibe.palette: A pale finish-post stands alone. Bad water is dark beneath the surface. No other marker stands anywhere on the course.
vibe.materials: No built structure stands here. Root and current carry the course entirely. A single carved post at the finish has names cut deep. The trial-keepers reset the water after each trial.

places.name: The Slow Ground

why.founding: Xanmeer footings sank into the mud here. The roots took the stone up again. A miregaunt walks the ground over the footings.
why.siteAdvantages: The mud is deep with hard courses under it. The miregaunt has footing there where a person has none.
why.occupantsMotive: The miregaunt keeps a circuit of about four hundred paces. It has not been seen off that ground.
why.pressures: Reed cutters worked this stand for three generations. They now cut a poorer stand a mile north. They say so loudly at market.
why.wouldChangeIf: Killing the miregaunt opens the good reed stand again.

preferences: off any walked path
a reed stand within sight

why.founding: A miregaunt has stood on the dry approach to Xal-Ussep. The wardens' line has known the ruin behind it for as long as the miregaunt has stood there. The miregaunt holds the approach.

vibe.silhouette: The approach looks like ground where the vegetation has been rearranged. The vegetation on the approach has been broken, not cleared.
vibe.palette: Green light skims the silt-white shallows. Root-wood has gone silver where the wet has bleached it. Old amber is crusted in the shade. A red flower stays still in the reflection.
vibe.materials: The approach ground is unworked. The vegetation on the approach is broken, not cleared. Weathered grey stone shows through the cut root. A single old totem marks the edge and has never been replaced. A debris band of gear lies sorted roughly by age.

places.name: The Held Mist

why.occupantsMotive: Whatever is in the hollow closes on visitors before it is seen. The guides route round the hollow. The guides charge clients as though they had crossed it.

vibe.silhouette: A standing mist body is visible from above. The mist fills this one hollow but not its neighbours.
vibe.palette: Grey mist lies over black water. Canopy green fades out past the rim. The bowl itself is drained of colour. A rope's pale line disappears downward.
vibe.materials: A single step is cut into living root. The step was made once and regretted. A rope anchor is tied off at the rim. Old paint marks on the last dry tree show the way out.
vibe.signatureFeature: Visibility inside the mist is under four metres in any weather. Local practice is to enter on a rope that is tied off outside.
vibe.condition: The hollow is left as it is. No repair has held for a season here.
vibe.mood: The hollow disorients visitors. Sounds from it carry far before it comes into view.
vibe.approach: The mist edge is a hard vertical line. A hand pushed into the mist disappears.
vibe.senses: Cold rises off the spring at the bottom. Sound arrives from a direction with nothing in it. Sight is gone within a few strides of the edge. Footsteps are lost past the mist line.

places.name: Waits-For-The-Second-Man

why.founding: A tribeless Naga band worked the plantation roads until the roads emptied. The band moved to the footpaths. Couriers still use the footpaths.
why.siteAdvantages: The camp lies on a thorn bank over a path. The path is narrow enough that a party has to walk it in single file.
why.occupantsMotive: The band takes the second walker in a line. The band lets the first walker pass. A party sees the loss only when it stops to count.
why.pressures: The nearest village now sends its couriers in fives. That leaves the band four more meals a day to win.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the bank shortens the courier run by a day.

hardConstraints: a walked footpath within two hundred metres

why.founding: The village exists to service the grave-pole fields of six neighbouring tribes.

places.name: Nine-Trunks

why.founding: A village grew where nine root-joined trunks stand in one ring. By the Hist's reckoning the ring is one tree. By the tribes' reckoning the ring is nine trees.
why.siteAdvantages: The ring encloses firm ground. The ring serves as its own stockade.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe hosts the convocation's overflow. The tribe has grown rich on hosting it. It rents pitch-rights to delegations that cannot fit at the Tsoko camp.
why.pressures: Hosting a province's delegations one month a year has made the tribe arrogant the other eleven. Two neighbouring tribes now choose to camp at Greenspring on principle.
why.wouldChangeIf: A convocation held elsewhere would halve the village. Attendance is counted publicly at the Root Talk ground. The falling attendance already shows in the village's rents.

sources: §12b Deepmire, the Refuge (a D4 destination with an approach route)

why.founding: The Kept Refuge is a shelter maintained on ground that the tribes avoid. The tribes keep it against the day they have to run again. The tribes ran in 4E 48.
why.siteAdvantages: The refuge stands high and dry. It is deliberately remote. It has one maintained approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Two caretakers serve the refuge on an unenvied rotation. The funding tribes draw the caretakers by lot. Each caretaker serves a year. The tribes accept no exemption.
why.pressures: The caretakers rotate the stores. The register of the year the refuge was full is read aloud. The reading happens every Sun's Dusk. Fewer tribes attend the reading each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Using the refuge would mean that something terrible had happened again. Two funding tribes have let their shares lapse. Neither tribe has said so at the reading.

preferences: water relation: above everything
neighbours: deliberately remote; an approach route exists and is maintained

notableNpcSlots.role: Keeper who has never turned anyone away

vibe.silhouette: A maintained structure stands on ground that has every reason to be empty.
vibe.palette: Tea-dark water lies under the canopy's shade. Sap runs treacle-dark into the collecting cups by the door. Churned pale mud marks the one maintained approach. Faded red paint shows on the entry posts.
vibe.materials: A canopy limb is bent down and rooted at both ends. The limb is roofed across the span. Hardwood pegs and withy hold the building together, with no metal. Bark shingle is laid fresh over the store-room roof. Stores are stacked to a marked capacity. The caretakers keep the stores up despite low use.
vibe.signatureFeature: A capacity mark on the wall reads 'four hundred and eleven, Sun's Dusk 4E 48'. The caretakers still keep stores for that many.
vibe.condition: The refuge is kept up on a rota. The repairs are small and recent.
vibe.mood: The mood is prepared. The refuge is short of attendance.
vibe.approach: A maintained roof is reached by the one cleared path.
vibe.senses: Heavy wet heat does not lift after dark. A counting voice reads aloud each Sun's Dusk. Otherwise the refuge is silent. The sweet-sour smell of green rot is held under the roof. No straight edge appears anywhere in the building's line.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can recount the stores. The stores are held against a forty-year-old survey. The recount must happen before the next flight needs the stores.

sources: hist-placement dossier (the continuous root layer); Lore:Rootworm; the province has almost no rock, so roots must carry the cave role

why.founding: The gallery began as a trunk root that died. The dead root gave way and collapsed.
why.siteAdvantages: The gallery lies on a route that people still use. People still dig at the fall because the route passes it.
why.occupantsMotive: The gallery is unoccupied. The bone-carriers come once a year. Four families' dead lie under the fall. The dead cannot be recovered and returned to their families.
why.pressures: The route now goes the long way around the fall. The detour costs a day. The porter relay charges for that day.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the fall would restore the route. It would also settle four families' claims. It would cost the relay yard a quarter of its traffic.

preferences: water relation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
neighbours: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect; that connection is the map
on the route it serves, close enough that traffic passes it

vibe.silhouette: The entrance is a slumped sinkhole lip. Old rope is still tied off at the edge. There is no safe way down.
vibe.palette: The passage is black past the entry. The old rope is pale against dark root. Green shows only where light still reaches the mouth.
vibe.materials: Nothing is built here. Packed silt lies over collapsed root and drift timber. The sinkhole lip is slumped, with rope still tied off at the edge. A porter train's load is still buried under two metres of fallen root.
vibe.signatureFeature: The gallery collapsed with a porter train inside it. The salvage is still where it fell. It lies behind two metres of root.
vibe.condition: The fall is untouched since it happened. People dig at it only from the outside.
vibe.mood: The place is a collapse with a burial inside it.
vibe.approach: The mouth is slumped. Fern has grown across the old path.
vibe.senses: The air past the entry sits still and close. A cold mineral smell comes off the deep mud. No sound carries back from where the tunnel closed.

playerPurpose.hook: A porter train is still under two metres of fallen root with its load. People are still digging toward it.

loot.provenance: stripped from earlier travellers

places.name: The Severed Branch
sources: hist-placement dossier (the continuous root layer); Lore:Rootworm; the province has almost no rock, so roots must carry the cave role

why.founding: A cult cell took the gallery. The roots here reach a tree that the cell intends to sever.
why.siteAdvantages: The gallery is isolated and deep. It connects directly to the cell's target.
why.occupantsMotive: Cultists are testing a method of severing. They work from notes that came out of the staging camp. They go back to the staging camp with their results.
why.pressures: The tree above the gallery is beginning to withdraw. The village does not know why the tree is withdrawing. The villagers have begun consulting a tree-minder. The tree-minder will recognise the pattern.
why.wouldChangeIf: Discovery would make the cell move. The cell would lose its notes. The notes are the written account of how a severing is actually attempted.

preferences: water relation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
neighbours: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect; that connection is the map

vibe.silhouette: The entrance is a grave-cut into the bank. The cut is too wide for one body. The approach marks are scrubbed off.
vibe.palette: The root is brown and lit only by carried lamps. Sap has gone dark and stiff along the cut marks. Grey silt dries at the entrance.
vibe.materials: The root walls are cut in a deliberate repeating pattern. The pattern is unlike any natural growth. A single step is cut into the bank for access. Notes are kept dry on a shelf inside.
vibe.signatureFeature: An Unbound Root cell has cut the root walls in a deliberate repeating pattern. The cell's notes explain the cuts.
vibe.condition: The cell keeps the entrance deliberately hidden. The cell scrubs the entrance clean of tracks.
vibe.approach: The approach marks at the mouth are scrubbed off.
vibe.senses: Chime notes at the entrance are pitched oddly to test anyone approaching. The smell of rot thickens near the mouth. Low argument is audible from within when work is under way. No natural light reaches past the first turn.
