places.name: The Long Throat
sources: hist-placement dossier (the continuous root layer); Lore:Rootworm; the province has almost no rock, so roots must carry the cave role

why.founding: The gallery is a single enormous trunk root. The root runs toward the basin.
why.siteAdvantages: The gallery is the dry way toward the deep basin.
why.occupantsMotive: No staff work inside the gallery. A guide camp sits at each end. The two camps keep a tally of everyone entering. The tally tells the far end who to expect.
why.pressures: A party cannot get back past whatever enters behind it. The guides move parties through in one direction only. The guides wait out the day if the tally is wrong.
why.wouldChangeIf: A branch collapse would turn the passage into a trap. A collapse would also cut the basin's deep ground off entirely.

preferences: water relation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
neighbours: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect; that connection is the map

vibe.silhouette: The entrance is a stair-throat of worn root steps going down a ravine wall. The first verse of the counting song is cut beside it.
vibe.palette: The passage is black and lit only by carried lamp. Grey silt dries in cracked plates along one stretch. The first counting verse is cut pale into stone at the mouth. The passage has no other colour for three kilometres.
vibe.materials: The passage is unworked root. No wall is built or repaired along its length. A traveller who reached the end left a single stake-cairn at one point. The counting verse is cut shallow into the stone lip at the entrance. That verse is the single mark made by any hand here. The root is otherwise as it grew.
vibe.signatureFeature: The gallery runs three kilometres without a side chamber or a branch. Travellers count paces aloud.
vibe.condition: The gallery is unchanged since it formed. It is unbuilt along its whole length.
vibe.mood: The passage is monotonous. It is long enough to be frightening.
vibe.approach: The mouth lies in a ravine wall. The first verse of the counting song is cut beside it.
vibe.senses: The low ceiling flattens the sound of footsteps. Every traveller murmurs a paced counting song along the passage. The air stays still for the whole length of the gallery.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 562 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.

playerPurpose.hook: The root run is three kilometres long. It has no junction and no side chamber. Travellers count paces aloud. Guides teach them the chant before they set off.

places.name: The Drowned Stair
sources: hist-placement dossier (the continuous root layer); Lore:Rootworm; the province has almost no rock, so roots must carry the cave role

why.founding: A root branch grew downhill into the water table.
why.siteAdvantages: The gallery short-cuts a full day of surface travel. Only a courier who can hold their breath can use it.
why.occupantsMotive: The gallery is uninhabited. Divers use it, mostly couriers. A message that takes a day on the surface takes an afternoon. The dive takes four held breaths.
why.pressures: The water rises in the wet season. The rising water drowns the last two landings. For half the year the shortcut is a full dive. The couriers charge double in that half.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry decade would make the gallery an ordinary road. A dry decade would end a courier trade. Three villages depend on that trade for news.

preferences: water relation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
neighbours: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect; that connection is the map
water relation: deep water at the mouth, the stair descending below it

places.traversalFallback: The fallback is to go by boat around the surface route. The boat route takes one day longer.

vibe.silhouette: No part of the gallery is above water. A diver finds the stair by feel. The entrance is made swimming.
vibe.palette: Lamp-yellow light fades to black in the depths. Grey drift-timber is wedged along the walls. The smooth-worn root carries no sap anywhere. Pale marks are cut fresh at each landing.
vibe.materials: The floor and ceiling are both root. Water carves the rest between them. The landing steps are cut and worn smooth by hundreds of passing feet. Grave-poles are driven at the rim. None of them is recent. No lashed or built work lies below the waterline.
vibe.signatureFeature: The gallery descends in flooded steps. Each step is a held breath longer than the last. The marks of who got how far are cut at each landing.
vibe.condition: The gallery is passable only in the dry season. The rest of the year it is drowned two landings deep.
vibe.mood: The place is a dive with a tally cut at every landing.
vibe.approach: The mouth lies at water level. Divers enter it swimming.
vibe.senses: Warm air rises strangely from underground. Divers hold their breath four times before the far landing. Sap has gone sour where the root has been cut. Sound is swallowed entirely below the surface.

playerPurpose.hook: A courier is through in an afternoon on four held breaths. The surface route takes a day. The marks of who got how far are cut at each landing.

loot.provenance: off the last party to try it

places.name: The Underway
sources: hist-placement dossier (the continuous root layer); Lore:Rootworm; the province has almost no rock, so roots must carry the cave role

why.founding: The gallery is the trunk root under Helstrom. The Waykeepers opened it and keep it as a road. The surface route crosses the deep basin.
why.siteAdvantages: The gallery goes where no boat can go. No road will be built where it goes.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers maintain the passage only as far as their contract runs. They post the paid limit in cut marks at the second junction.
why.pressures: Beyond the second junction the passage is not maintained. People still go beyond it. The Waykeepers have stopped recovering bodies past the second junction. The Waykeepers have not told the assembly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the Waykeepers would close the interior's overland link entirely. Helstrom's escorted water traffic could not absorb the difference.

preferences: water relation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
neighbours: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect; that connection is the map

notableNpcSlots.role: The line-keeper holds the post at the Helstrom mouth.

vibe.silhouette: The entrance is a worked gate in the root wall at the Helstrom line. The gate is lit and guarded. Traffic queues at the gate.
vibe.palette: The passage is black past the lamp's reach. Mud is churned underfoot. Amber is set hard in the root joints. Passing walkers leave red flowers in wall niches.
vibe.materials: The tunnel's own walls are root, black silt and old bone. A maintained gate stands at the Helstrom mouth. Cut marks post the paid limit at the second junction. A traveller who found the way out left a stake-cairn.
vibe.signatureFeature: The Waykeepers maintain the floor and hang lights as far as the second junction. The Waykeepers' contract ends at the second junction.
vibe.condition: The floor is laid and lit to the paid limit. Beyond the paid limit there is root and water.
vibe.mood: The passage is comfortable underground. It is unlike the rest of the region.
vibe.approach: The mouth is a worn root mouth at the Helstrom gate. A keeper's post stands there. A written notice states how far the maintenance goes.
vibe.senses: Trapped air presses close and still. Insects sound inside the walls. A rot-sweet smell hangs past the second junction. The passage has no straight line anywhere.

places.name: The Kept Light

why.founding: The gallery lies under a hammock that dropped its levee. The water came in from the back and stayed.
why.siteAdvantages: The run holds chest-deep still water in the dark. One dry shelf lies at the far end. Two mouths open at opposite ends of the run.
why.occupantsMotive: Wisps hold a light over the deepest cut. A wader is in leech water before it is halfway to the light.
why.pressures: Two polers from the eastern hamlets have gone in after the light this year. Their rafts are still tied at the root mouth.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting the old levee back open would drain the run to ankle depth. The wisps would go when the run drains.

hardConstraints: a failed levee or a dropped hammock edge
preferences: off any walked path
standing water at the mouth

vibe.silhouette: The entrance is a root mouth at water level. Two empty rafts are tied to it.
vibe.palette: Black water lies under one small blue light deep in the run. Brown root walls close overhead. Pale poling gear lies abandoned on the rafts. No colour shows anywhere the light does not reach.
vibe.materials: Living and drowned root together form the gallery walls. Two rafts are tied at the mouth with their poling gear still aboard. A dry shelf at the far end is the only footing in the run. The gallery itself is the sole structure. Nothing else is built here.
vibe.signatureFeature: The light sits over a cut where the floor drops away.
vibe.condition: The gallery holds. The levee behind it does not hold.
vibe.approach: The drip carries before the mouth is in sight.

why.founding: Growers took over the root gallery. They needed dark, damp and constant temperature.
why.siteAdvantages: The root layer provides dark, damp and constant temperature for free.
why.occupantsMotive: The growers are underground by preference. They rarely surface. They sell glowing fungus to every village in the district. They sell through a single agent.
why.pressures: Something else uses the deeper branches. The growers have stopped going to the deeper branches. Their best beds are out of production. The price of the fungus is up.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would end the interior's light supply. The nightbound village uses none of the fungus.

preferences: water relation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
neighbours: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect; that connection is the map

vibe.silhouette: The entrance is a hollow trunk. A fungus-drying rack stands outside it. A tended path leads to it.
vibe.palette: The fungus-lit walls glow pale green. A drying rack shows pale against dark root-brown. Mud-grey banks lie at the entrance.
vibe.materials: The growers fitted out the hollow trunk with drying racks themselves. Fungus beds are cut directly into the root walls. Daily traffic has worn the tended path smooth.
vibe.signatureFeature: A small community colonised the gallery. They farm luminous fungus on the root walls. They sell light to the villages above.
vibe.condition: The growers who live there keep the gallery in daily repair.
vibe.approach: A tended path leads to the mouth. A fungus-drying rack stands outside the mouth.
vibe.senses: The warmth is damp and constant, unlike the surface. A faint mushroom smell hangs over standing water. Chimes sound distant down the gallery. Each chime is a little out of tune with the last.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can move the growers' jarred light past the assembly's licences.

sources: docs/quests/20-world-provisions.md §12b (the great Root Talk at Helstrom)
§12b owner decision Q2 (the great Root Talk is an occasion, not a council); Lore:Hist-Tsoko

why.founding: The Root Talk is an occasional convocation held at Helstrom. The convocation falls in the month of Hist-Tsoko.
why.siteAdvantages: The ground is an enclosed clearing at the grove's edge. Enclosed clearings like this are rare. The clearing holds every interior delegation and their landings.
why.occupantsMotive: The ground stands empty for eleven months in twelve. In the twelfth month the naheesh and tree-minders of the interior sit here. The seating is set by a precedence order that is kept at Helstrom.
why.pressures: Attendance at the Root Talk is falling. The empty places are counted publicly. Two tribes have stopped coming. The two tribes have not been asked why in six years.
why.wouldChangeIf: A convocation that failed to reach alignment would end the institution. The residents of the Hist-less refuge are waiting for that end. The heretic builders are waiting for that end as well.

preferences: water relation: landings for delegations
neighbours: at or beside a hero Hist or a capital

notableNpcSlots.role: Naheesh who holds this year's Root Talk

vibe.silhouette: The ground is very large and cleared. It has permanent stone or root seating, but it has no buildings.
vibe.palette: The pale root is worn to a shine underfoot. Green shade lies overhead. A single red flower is shed and left where it falls.
vibe.materials: Root is trained flat over generations into floor and seating. None of the root is cut. One chime frame stands at the north end. A standing rule forbids building here.
vibe.signatureFeature: Generations have worn the root seating into shape. Each tribe's delegation mark is cut where that tribe has sat since the seating was trained. The recently unclaimed marks are obvious.
vibe.condition: The ground is not repaired by hand. Its upkeep comes from growth and custom.
vibe.approach: A worn path runs from the Helstrom gate. The path is a highway for one month a year. The path is a green tunnel for the rest of the year.
vibe.senses: The floor hums when many feet cross the ground at once. The ground is quiet for eleven months of the year. Resin scent from the grove drifts in from the edge. One voice speaks at a time during the convocation.

places.name: The Emptied Bore
sources: Lore:Rootworm (eight feet, translucent, digests very slowly)

why.founding: A rootworm dug this bore. The worm died in the bore. The bore was then abandoned.
why.siteAdvantages: The tunnel is dry, wide and straight. Dry shelter is extremely rare here.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever creature is living in a free tunnel occupies the bore. The occupant changes every season. No village has claimed the bore.
why.pressures: Travellers want to use the bore as shelter. Something is usually in it already. The bore has killed more travellers than the weather ever drove into it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the bore would give the region a dry way-shelter. The guides have costed the work twice. The guides cannot agree who would own the bore afterwards.

preferences: water relation: dry root ground
neighbours: on or beside the root-transit network, where the Waykeepers' line runs past it

vibe.silhouette: The bore mouth is old and oval where it has slumped. Ferns grow across the opening.
vibe.palette: The mouth is round and dark, fringed with fern. The tunnel walls are brown-black and smoothed to a shine. Pale worm bone fills the last chamber. Old cut marks have gone hard and dark with age.
vibe.materials: The bore is unlined. The worm cut the bore itself. The bore has never been reinforced. Ferns grow unchecked across the collapsed mouth. The worm's skeleton fills the last forty metres. The skeleton is untouched since the worm died there. No shelter work has been added since.
vibe.signatureFeature: The worm's skeleton fills the last chamber that it dug. The tunnel stops at that chamber.
vibe.condition: The mouth is slumped shut. Clearing it has not been agreed.
vibe.approach: The bore is a perfectly round dry hole in a bank. It is too neat to be natural.
vibe.senses: Cold air pools at the tunnel floor even in the dry season. Old fern fronds rattle dryly at the entrance. A faint carrion smell never quite clears from the last chamber.

places.name: The Working Burrow
sources: Lore:Rootworm (eight feet, translucent, digests very slowly)

why.founding: A wild rootworm dug this burrow off a trunk root. The Waykeepers watch the burrow. A wild worm can open or close a line.
why.siteAdvantages: The burrow lies where soft ground meets the root layer. The worm can turn at that point.
why.occupantsMotive: A rootworm lives in the burrow. A small scavenger population lives off the worm's spoil. The Waykeepers read this ecology well. They can predict where the worm will turn.
why.pressures: The Waykeepers want the worm moved. The local tribe considers it sacred. The dispute has been at the convocation twice. The convocation gave no ruling.
why.wouldChangeIf: Driving the worm off would open a shorter root line. It would also start an argument that would reach Helstrom.

preferences: water relation: dry root ground
neighbours: on or beside the root-transit network, where the Waykeepers' line runs past it

vibe.silhouette: The burrow mouth is ringed with cut root. The mouth is wider than a gallery. The spoil ridge is still fresh.
vibe.palette: Wet root walls show a lamp-yellow sheen. Freshly turned spoil ridges are pale. Thin sap beads along the tunnel cuts. A single red flower lies crushed flat at the mouth.
vibe.materials: The burrow floor is root that a moving body has packed hard. Water shapes the rest of the burrow. A spoil ridge of turned earth lies loose at the mouth. A stone-and-pole cairn stands where the last person got out. No built structure stands inside.
vibe.signatureFeature: Fresh spoil heaps lie outside the mouth. The mouth is wider than any maintained gallery. The rim of the mouth is worn smooth.
vibe.condition: The Waykeepers and the tribe dispute the burrow. It is left as the worm made it.
vibe.mood: The worm is felt through the ground before it is heard.
vibe.approach: The ground shakes at irregular intervals. The shaking begins a long way off.
vibe.senses: The ground trembles before any sound arrives. Turned earth and torn root fill the air. Sap sours where the fresh cuts leak. There is no dry footing near the mouth.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 383 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, danger, parent.

why.founding: The station is the hub of the rootworm network (root-node.helstrom).
why.siteAdvantages: The station stands at the Helstrom gate. The trunk roots converge there.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers run the station. They run a semi-public service and a restricted one. A paying passenger is not told that the restricted network exists. The register has two columns.
why.pressures: The restricted network is a favour. It is not a service. The Waykeepers guard it as a favour. The tribes of the interior have begun to resent a road whose inside they may not see.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the Waykeepers' cooperation closes the interior. The Waykeepers know this. They price accordingly.

preferences: water relation: dry root ground
neighbours: nodes on the root network; not on any map

places.name: The Bleeding House
sources: Lore:Haj Uxith (Molag Bal's sap harvest); Lore:Hist Sap

why.founding: A Daedric-worked facility was built in the interior. It harvests a Hist industrially. It follows the Haj Uxith pattern.
why.siteAdvantages: The facility stands on a tree. It does not stand on ground. The building is a machine that wraps around a trunk.
why.occupantsMotive: The bargain left something there. That something still works the machine on a schedule. No tribe has authorised anyone to enter the building for six hundred years.
why.pressures: The tree is still alive. It is still connected. Its anguish is felt down the root line. The Agaceph sap-speaker can name the direction of the anguish. The sap-speaker has refused three times.
why.wouldChangeIf: Ending the facility would be the largest thing that the interior has done in a century. The convocation rarely reaches agreement. It would agree to reward this act.

preferences: water relation: isolated
neighbours: deliberately avoided by every route and every village

vibe.silhouette: The facility is industrial apparatus on a Hist. The manufacture is not from Tamriel.
vibe.palette: Lamp-yellow light catches wet black stone. Sap-channels stain every wall dark red-brown. One steady red glow shows. It is not a flower. Grey silt coats every floor.
vibe.materials: Dressed stone is fused with worked daedric metal. It is the only metal for a hundred miles. Sap-channels are cut straight into the floor and still run. Root has grown into the machinery. The root died where it touched the machinery. Portable fittings were stripped out long ago. The fixed apparatus was left standing.
vibe.signatureFeature: The apparatus is still running, unattended. The sap that it collects has gone the wrong colour.
vibe.condition: The apparatus runs unattended. It has run to its schedule for six centuries.
vibe.approach: The root-hum in this region carries a wrong note for kilometres. The source is found last.
vibe.senses: Warm air rises off the tree-body and carries its sap-scent. A mechanical drip keeps time too evenly to be natural. Sap turns sour and then metallic near the collecting vats. There is no chime and no birdcall. The only sound is the machine's own working.

why.occupantsMotive: Tappers work here. Their licence is their livelihood. They police poachers themselves. An unpoliced district loses its licences entirely.
why.pressures: The licence is renewed annually. The objection comes most reliably from the tribe whose tree carried the stage the previous year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A lost licence would be worth violence. The last holder to lose one now sells to the same city fence as the poachers.

places.name: Miredance

why.founding: The sap-touched left together in one season. They walked out in the slow shared rhythm that they had kept for years.
why.siteAdvantages: The root system of the overflow pool had hollowed a gallery beneath the huts. The dancers only ever lived on top of the gallery.
why.occupantsMotive: No household is kept here now. Creatures that came for the standing water moved into the root galleries. The creatures have not been driven out.
why.pressures: The tap-lines above ground still run when sap flows from the tree. They feed the pool. Whatever lives below is drawn to the pool.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the overflow dried, the gallery would dry with it. The gallery would lose whatever nests there now.

hardConstraints: at least 1.5 km from the province edge

neighbours: other villages keep their distance

vibe.palette: Green shade has gone to black mould over standing water. Sap dried black over the old tap cuts. No other colour is left.
vibe.materials: Grafted limbs collapsed where the joints gave way. Tap-lines still sag above the pool. Drums hang at the stage, split with damp.
vibe.signatureFeature: The drums are still hung at the tap-lines. The drums are split and swollen with damp.
vibe.condition: The site is abandoned above ground. The gallery below is undisturbed.
vibe.approach: The drums used to carry before the huts came into view. Now the drums are heard only at the root-mouth.
vibe.senses: Cold air rises out of the root-mouth below. A drumbeat is heard only at the mouth and never above. Standing sap has gone sour. The frog-pipe is not heard anywhere near the pool.

places.name: Xal-Ussep
sources: Lore:Xanmeer (~25% sealed; vakka stones); Lore:Vakka Stone

why.founding: Xal-Ussep is a xanmeer that was sealed with its tribe's Hist inside it. The Hist has been alone since the Duskfall.
why.siteAdvantages: Xal-Ussep stands on firm ground in tropical jungle, 7.8 m from swamp water. The xanmeer was never opened.
why.occupantsMotive: Only the Hist tree lives inside Xal-Ussep. The tree has not touched the collective since the Duskfall. The tree may not know that the Duskfall has ended.
why.pressures: A whole tribe watches Xal-Ussep. None of its members has ever been inside. The watch post holds that tribe together now.
why.wouldChangeIf: Opening Xal-Ussep would release or kill a Hist that has been isolated for an age. It is the nearest thing to a test of whether a tree can be cut off from the collective and live.

preferences: water relation: raised, often ringed by marsh
neighbours: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it

vibe.silhouette: Xal-Ussep is a small, entirely intact stepped meer. It has a single stair-throat. Warm air comes out of the stair-throat.
vibe.palette: The stone is dressed grey and is unweathered by the centuries. A single bright green thread of root runs through a crack in the wall. Gold light with no fire source shows deep inside the stair. Dark unlit chambers lie beyond the seal.
vibe.materials: The quarried stone was sealed at every joint on the day the meer was shut. No joint has been reopened since. A living trunk has grown against the inside of the chamber ceiling. A root pushes three metres through the outer wall. The stone doors are still seated true. No repair has ever been made, because none has been needed.
vibe.signatureFeature: A living Hist is sealed inside the stone. The trunk has grown into the chamber's ceiling. A root has come out through the wall. Three metres of tree are visible from outside.
vibe.condition: Xal-Ussep has been sealed since the Duskfall. It has never been opened or repaired.
vibe.mood: The meer is sealed and warm. A presence inside answers a visitor.
vibe.approach: The root through the wall shows that Xal-Ussep is not an empty ruin.
vibe.senses: Warm air breathes steadily out of a stair that should hold no heat. A low resonant hum is felt through the stone floor before it is heard. Total silence holds here, where every other xanmeer carries some sound.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can reach the sealed Hist or keep it sealed. A quest can also bring the questing party before the watch for trying.

heroHist.note: Hero Hist 9/10. Sealed xanmeer Hist — alive, walled into its own Hist chamber and alone for millennia. Power slot granted only on release. hist-placement §3 caps living sealed trees at two or three province-wide.

places.reconciliation: Xal-Ussep is among the 2–3 living sealed Hist allowed province-wide. Its neighbours must claim at most two more living sealed Hist.

localStateVariants.whatChanges: In the sealed state, the stair-throat is shut. The hum is felt only outside.

localStateVariants.when: This state applies after the chamber is opened.
localStateVariants.whatChanges: In the opened state, the living tree can be reached. Its sap-glow lights the interior.

places.name: The Coiling Reach

why.founding: The Coiling Reach is a reach where the big snakes den in the root banks.
why.siteAdvantages: The root banks are warm and sit above the flood line. Those are the conditions that snakes need for a den.
why.occupantsMotive: Giant snakes live here. Hunters take them for hide. The daril fermentary sets the hunting season. The snakes do not set it.
why.pressures: Snake hide is worth enough that hunters keep coming and keep dying. The daril fermentary buys venom from the same reach. A bad year hits both the hide trade and the venom trade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Overhunting would clear the reach of snakes in a decade. The daril fermentary has begun keeping its own stock against that day.

preferences: water relation: dry basking ground near water
neighbours: avoided ground between routes

vibe.silhouette: Shed skins hang at a size that halts an approach.
vibe.palette: Green fades to blue-grey in standing mist. Pale shed skins drape high in the branches. The amber has long since drained from the buckets. A red flower lies flattened in a drag mark.
vibe.materials: Repeated denning has warmed and hollowed the root banks. The turning of heavy coils has polished the floor smooth. The hunters' rope stands are lashed to the nearest firm trunk. A single old totem marks the edge of the range.
vibe.signatureFeature: Sloughed skins hang in the branches. Hunters left them there as range markers.
vibe.condition: Hunters work the reach every season for hide. At other times the snakes hold the reach as they please.
vibe.approach: The skins first.
vibe.senses: Musk and dry skin hang thick in the warm air. Leaf litter ferments underfoot, sweet and sharp. A long hiss carries further than any bird call. The stillness breaks when a coil shifts.

places.name: The Swallow

why.pressures: The tribes fence the rim. Something breaks the fence from the inside every year. The fence has been rebuilt eleven times.
why.wouldChangeIf: A second collapse would open the hollow into the root layer below. The Waykeepers' second junction lies directly beneath it.

vibe.materials: The rim is fenced with driven stakes that face outward. A rope ladder is rigged and cut short at four metres. A single totem stands at the fence line and has not been renewed for years.

places.name: Sleeps-In-The-Ring

why.founding: The tribe kept a hundred-year vigil over a hist that had gone to sleep. The village was built in a ring around a xanmeer that is older than the vigil.
why.siteAdvantages: Sleeps-In-The-Ring stands on firm ground, 5.5 m from a lagoon. The rise was defensible and dry. The tribe did not ask what lay under the rise.
why.occupantsMotive: A presence that slept under the xanmeer woke enough to be noticed. The village had waited ninety years for its own tree to wake. The villagers left in a single night, when something else woke instead.
why.pressures: The hatchery pool goes unswept. The stair-throat down into the xanmeer has been open since the village was left.
why.wouldChangeIf: The presence that woke below must sleep again or be killed. Only then could the tribe live in the ring again.

water relation: a rise ringed by pond water

vibe.silhouette: A ring of collapsed roofs surrounds a stair-throat. The stair-throat is sunk into old xanmeer stone.
vibe.palette: Tea-black water has gone grey under thin canopy. Amber sap has dried hard and dark on the collapsed roofs. Pale xanmeer stone shows at the stair mouth. There is no red anywhere in the ring.

why.founding: One household lives in a xanmeer antechamber because the antechamber was empty and dry.

why.pressures: The tribe that tends the xanmeer knows about the family and has not decided what to do. Evicting the family would mean admitting that the antechamber was habitable.

places.name: The Standing Thing

why.founding: What the Standing Thing is and who made it are unknown. The local tribes tell four incompatible stories about it.
why.siteAdvantages: Vegetation has grown around the Standing Thing without touching it.
why.occupantsMotive: None of the four tribes has ever posted a custodian. A presence below the stone has kept the two-metre circle clear without help.
why.pressures: Two of the four stories are politically useful and are being pushed. One story makes the stone Ayleid, which would open a dig. Another story makes it pre-Duskfall Argonian, which would close a dig for good.
why.wouldChangeIf: An authoritative answer would disappoint three of the four stories. The Helstrom assembly has declined to hear the question three times.

preferences: water relation: varies
neighbours: deliberately unrelated to its surroundings

vibe.silhouette: The object is unmistakably made. It is unmistakably wrong for its surroundings.
vibe.palette: Worked grey stone stands against a quarter-mile of reed. A single red flower lies on the stone. Churned mud lies at the circle's edge.
vibe.materials: A single dressed stone stands, unlike anything quarried nearby. A scatter of totems lies at the rim and has been untouched since the last flood. There is no roof, no wall and no second stone.
vibe.signatureFeature: Vegetation stops dead at a two-metre radius around the stone. It has done so since the grave-singers began keeping the count.
vibe.condition: The stone is unclaimed and untended. It holds only as long as the next season allows.
vibe.mood: The stone is unexplained. The circle stays clear.
vibe.approach: A circle of bare earth lies in country that grows over a cut in a season.
vibe.senses: Ground is bare here, where growth returns to any other cut within a season. An old chime frame is left unclaimed. Ash mixed with sap lies at the circle's edge. No sound carries from directly overhead.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can settle one of the four incompatible stories. A quest can also leave all four standing.

places.name: Two-Poles

why.founding: Two-Poles is a hamlet-turned-village on a shallow flat. The flat floods to the floor twice a year. The village is rebuilt each time.
why.siteAdvantages: The shallow flat has good fishing and no competition.
why.occupantsMotive: The families have decided that the rebuild is cheaper than moving. They have made the rebuild a rite. It takes three days with the whole village present.
why.pressures: The floods are getting deeper. The piles are getting longer. The timber now comes from the hammock village, which charges for it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Two bad years running would end the village. The households have not agreed where they would go. The firm ground nearby is a rise that is already fully occupied.

preferences: water relation: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
neighbours: strung along a waterway, linear not radial

vibe.silhouette: Two mooring poles stand well out from a short pile line. They are visible before the village is.
vibe.palette: Two bare mooring poles stand pale against brown water. Root-scarred pile stumps from earlier villages ring the current one. Fish-scale silver shows on the drying racks. Red flower petals darken on wet boards.
vibe.materials: Piles are driven fresh after every flood. The shortest stumps from four earlier rebuilds stay standing as markers. Walls are split cane lashed with new withy each season. Roofs are re-thatched from reed cut at the flat itself. Nothing here is older than the last flood, by design.
vibe.signatureFeature: Pile stumps from four earlier villages stand around the current one in the shallows. The stumps read like a diagram of the village's own history.
vibe.condition: The village is rebuilt as a rite. Each flood brings three days of work.
vibe.approach: The old stumps read as a ruin from the water. The living village is behind them.
vibe.senses: Fish and wet cane scent every board. The whole structure rocks gently underfoot with the current. A frog-pipe is practised somewhere under the piles.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can go down into what each of the four earlier villages left.

why.siteAdvantages: The channel edge has a bed firm enough to pile. The bank is high enough for landing.
why.occupantsMotive: Polers and provisioners live in Ux-Aneet. They live off passing convoys. Helstrom's escort schedule sets their margins.
why.pressures: The convoys are escorted and often pass without stopping. The escorts prefer Greenspring, which has cleaner water. Greenspring's tribe flatters the escorts.
why.wouldChangeIf: A change in the escorted route would empty Ux-Aneet in two years. The village has begun courting the pilgrim traffic as a hedge.

preferences: water relation: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
neighbours: strung along a waterway, linear not radial

vibe.silhouette: A long low deck follows one channel bend. All the huts stand on the outside of the curve.
vibe.palette: Brown channel water reflects green overhang. Pale root-wood decking is worn silvery at the edges. Red flower petals are trodden soft into the boards. White bone charms hang at eye height.
vibe.materials: Stilt piles of root are grown deliberately round the older frame. Withy lashing is renewed on every joint each wet season. The patched frond roofing has not been repaired since the last storm. Forty tin chimes hang, with a single chime to each door.
vibe.signatureFeature: Every house has its own landing ladder. Every house has its own toll board. The toll boards disagree with each other.
vibe.condition: Working polers keep the village solid. It is defended mostly by being hard to reach.

why.pressures: The canopy has grown and the sightline is closing. The reading is disputed. The tribes that dispute the reading are the ones that would prefer not to attend.

why.pressures: Treasure hunters do not accept that maintenance means ownership. The living outfit nearby has twice offered the tribe a share to look away.

places.name: The Cut Circle

why.founding: The hall is a stilt hall built for a village that did not grow. People who wanted a room where two hundred could sit uncounted took it over.

why.occupantsMotive: The Unbound Root preach here openly. They preach to people who arrive believing something milder than what will be asked of them.
why.pressures: Preaching in public is how the cult recruits. It is also how the cult will eventually be found. The congregation is not the cell, but most of the congregation does not know this.
why.wouldChangeIf: One arrest in the middle of a sermon empties the hall for good. Two hundred people would then have to say what they heard.

hardConstraints: over deep still water on piles
preferences: no sightline from any route

vibe.palette: The timber is unpainted grey and warm lamplight slats through split cane walls. Black open water lies beneath the floor. The cut root lies pale the length of the hall.
vibe.materials: The hall is unornamented pile and plank construction with split cane walls left free of paint and carving, built for a village that never grew into it. vibe.approach: The causeway is the sole approach. The watch counts each arrival along it.

places.name: Still-Waiting
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/argonia-4e201-state.md (the Wild Ones; the promised clean province)

why.founding: The vigil families kept faith for a hundred and fifty years. A sickness went through the settlement in one wet season. The sickness took most of the vigil families.
why.siteAdvantages: The enclosed clearing once gave the vigil dry ground. The same clearing leaves the root warren below it dark and undisturbed.
why.occupantsMotive: No household keeps Still-Waiting now. Something moved into the collapsed cellars after the houses emptied. It came up through the root-mouth.
why.pressures: Tally stones are still stacked at the swept ground. They have been uncounted since the year the sickness came.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the warren would allow the tally to be finished. The tally-keeper has not entered the warren.

hardConstraints: ground defensible enough to have been chosen in a panic
preferences: water relation: minor
a purification site 200-400 m off, still swept

vibe.silhouette: Sunken roofs mark the village. A root-mouth stands where the swept ground used to be.
vibe.palette: Grey rot lies over the sunken roofing. Root has gone black at the collapsed cellars. One fleck of bone shows pale in the leaf litter.
vibe.materials: Root growth has pulled down the cane walls. Old grass-rope ties are still knotted on fallen posts. Tally stones are stacked in sets of ten at the swept ground.
vibe.signatureFeature: The tally stones are stacked in sets of ten. The stacks stop mid-count at the year of the sickness.
vibe.condition: The tally has been uncounted since the sickness took the households.
vibe.mood: The village is quiet. The houses are empty.
vibe.approach: The swept ground shows under the leaf litter before the roofline does.
vibe.senses: Root smell hangs over standing rot. No birds sing this close to the warren mouth. Leaf litter shifts somewhere below the roofline. The swept ground stays readable before the ruin does.

places.singularClaim: Still-Waiting has countBand [1,1]. One plague-abandoned village is a tragedy. Several would be a movement. The An-Xileel withdrawal order was a single event.
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 395 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.

playerPurpose.hook: The vigil lasted a hundred and fifty years. A sickness ended the vigil in one wet season. Something has since come up through the root-mouth into the cellars.

loot.provenance: left by the people who lived here
whatever the current occupants have taken

places.name: High Crossing
sources: asset inventory (the passerelles walkway kit: curving, climbing, branching); Lore:Murkmire

why.founding: Four walkway routes are forced to meet. They meet above ground that floods to chest height.
why.siteAdvantages: High Crossing is the single place where the four alignments can share a footing.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper collects for maintenance and sells rope. The keeper knows the true condition of all four arms. The tribes that pay him do not know it.
why.pressures: Four tribes use High Crossing. Two of the tribes pay for it. The branching village a day away has the same problem. That village has started coordinating rates.
why.wouldChangeIf: If one arm fails, the traffic of an entire tribe is rerouted. The Paatru are the tribe most likely to be affected. The Paatru have no alternative that does not cross their own mire.

preferences: water relation: over water throughout
neighbours: connects three or more water settlements

vibe.silhouette: The walkway lines converge. They can be seen across open marsh.
vibe.palette: Silt-white water catches green light below the deck. Pale sand shows at the channel turn. A gold bead of sap hangs on the underside of a limb. No red shows on this tree.
vibe.materials: Root is braided tight into the deck's frame like basketwork. Flint-vine cord lashes every joint. Sap-rubber gaskets seal the small store box. A maintenance ledger is nailed to the central post.
vibe.signatureFeature: The four-way deck stands at head height. A maintenance ledger is nailed to the post. The ledger lists who paid and who did not.
vibe.condition: The keeper shores up the deck only at the points that the ledger lists as needing it.
vibe.approach: Four walkway lines converge over open marsh.
vibe.senses: The deck is audible before it comes into view. Insect noise is thick against the braided walls. Sap sours at the cut edges nearby. The surrounding green absorbs the crossing's echo quickly.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest can buy the keeper's knowledge of the four arms. A quest can test that knowledge.
questHooks.tierOwnership: MR06 · tier-2; LH32 · tier-3; LH34 · tier-3

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 64 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

playerPurpose.hook: Four routes meet at head height. They meet over ground that floods to the chest. The ledger on the post lists who paid and who did not.

loot.provenance: left for the next traveller, by shelter custom

places.name: The Charged Pond
sources: docs/quests/20-world-provisions.md §12b (wamasu electrify the water around them)
Lore:Wamasu; Lore:Haynekhtnamet (received offerings to stay the flooding)

why.founding: The Charged Pond is a wamasu nesting pond. The tribes avoid it. The guar herds avoid it.
why.siteAdvantages: The pond holds still, deep, isolated water. That kind of water suits nesting.
why.occupantsMotive: A breeding pair and a season's eggs live here. Buyers in the coastal egg trade would pay a fortune for the eggs. No interior guide will lead a party here.
why.pressures: The water is lethal to swim while the wamasu are in it. The route past has to go round. The detour runs through the marsh giant's expanding range.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the pond opens a two-hour shortcut. Clearing it ends a species' nest site. The offering-shrine keepers hold that the flood-staying rite depends on the pair being there.

preferences: water relation: a held pond, still and avoided
neighbours: a district hazard; villages route around it

vibe.silhouette: Dead standing trees show lightning scarring. The fish have left the pond.
vibe.palette: Dead lightning-scarred trunks stand pale against brown water. A ring of dead fish floats pale at the surface. No red shows anywhere near the pond.
vibe.materials: There is no structure of any kind. Bare root and flood debris pile at the upstream edge. A single depth stick stands in the bank. The pond is still because of the nesting pair's presence.
vibe.signatureFeature: Dead fish float in a ring at the radius of the discharge. The ring is renewed daily.
vibe.condition: The pond is not visited, by rule as much as by fear.
vibe.approach: The dead ring is visible before the animals are.
vibe.senses: The water sits unnaturally still until something moves under it. The ring of dead fish gives off a sweet rot smell. The smell is renewed daily. The heavy silence is broken by surface ripples alone.

playerPurpose.hook: Dead fish float in a ring at the radius of the discharge. The ring is renewed daily. Past the ring the route is two hours shorter.

creatures.note: hatchlings in the shallows, already carrying a charge

loot.provenance: nesting stock that nothing else approaches

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 302 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; needs 1 m of water.

places.name: The Struck Ground

why.founding: The Struck Ground is a shallow pan of warm standing water. The pan lies on black mud and has no outfall. Adult wamasu have wallowed in it since before the nearest village kept a count.
why.siteAdvantages: The banks are soft. The water is deep enough to wallow. From the middle of the pan the tree line is clearly visible.
why.occupantsMotive: Three grown wamasu hold the water. They drive off whatever comes to drink. They drive off each other's young.
why.pressures: The village two hours east lost a lizard-steed at the pan last dry season. Its hunters now walk round by the reed cut. The detour costs them half a morning.
why.wouldChangeIf: Killing the big male opens the water again. Another adult moves into the pan before the year is out.

preferences: off any walked path
soft ground for the whole approach

vibe.silhouette: The pan is flat and brown with three long backs in it. Dead trees stand round the rim. The water killed their roots.
vibe.palette: The water is flat and brown. Grey standing deadwood lines the rim. Pale wamasu bellies turn in the shallows.
vibe.materials: Soft black mud lies underfoot for two hundred paces before open water. Drowned timber rings the pan. A lizard-steed's saddle lies abandoned on the bank.
vibe.signatureFeature: The air over the pan smells burnt on a still day.
vibe.condition: The ground is unbuilt. Wallowing has produced its present form.
vibe.approach: The ground softens for two hundred paces before the water shows.
vibe.senses: Flies work the mudline. A crack and a burnt smell come when a wamasu shifts its bulk. Warm still air lies over the pan. No birdcall sounds over the open water.

questHooks.opportunity: A village that wants its drinking pan back must decide which of the three wamasu it can afford to leave alive.

playerPurpose.hook: Three grown wamasu share one warm pan. Charged bone is worth carrying out.

loot.provenance: charged bone and scale cut from the wallow, plus the saddle on the bank

places.name: The Root Fall
sources: scour: 60 waterfall candidates (capped), concentrated on the rim; openworld research (concealment as a gate)

why.founding: A spring bursts out of the root layer. It falls into a chamber behind the curtain.
why.siteAdvantages: The fall has twenty metres of vertical relief. Such relief is rare in this country.
why.occupantsMotive: The chamber is used by whatever needs a dry room behind water. In this district it has held a cult cell, a smuggler and something else. The village downstream describes that something only as an animal.
why.pressures: The village downstream knows a chamber lies behind the fall. The villagers stopped counting who came back two naheesh ago.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry season halves the curtain. The halved curtain exposes the entrance. Whoever uses the chamber then has to move.

preferences: water relation: behind falling water
neighbours: on a river with real relief — the rim and upland only

vibe.silhouette: The fall itself is a visible cue. The chamber is not visible.
vibe.palette: Grey-brown mud curls dry at the chamber edge. A single bright line of gold sap runs down the root wall. A red Hist flower grows high in the canopy above the fall. Black water pounds pale where it breaks.
vibe.materials: Living root lines the chamber walls. The chamber has no stone lining. The root is warm to the touch. A previous visitor left one rope tied off and never retrieved it. Raw mud is packed into the gaps where the root does not meet flush. Nothing here has been shaped, only used.
vibe.signatureFeature: The fall comes out of a living root. It does not come out of rock. The chamber behind it is lined with the same root. The chamber is warm and dry.
vibe.condition: New rope hangs beside work three lifetimes old. The chamber has not been claimed by any occupant.
vibe.mood: The chamber is a hidden room in country with almost no rock.
vibe.approach: The noise carries two kilometres through closed canopy.
vibe.senses: The roar of falling water carries for two kilometres through closed canopy. Still warm air fills the chamber. Cold spray fills the chamber's mouth. Wet mud underfoot smells of minerals.

places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 157 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, culture-clump, landform.

playerPurpose.hook: The fall comes out of a living root. It does not come out of rock. The chamber behind it is warm, dry and root-lined.

loot.provenance: what one family owned and left

terrainRequests.note: the root-layer spring needs a drop to fall down and a chamber behind the curtain; the region has no natural relief

places.name: The Panther Race
sources: region grammar: deep river corridor; Lore:Seafalls; the arterial class needs its own hazards

why.founding: The Panther fork drops through a root-choked reach. The reach is the Panther Race.
why.siteAdvantages: The Panther Race is fast water. The province is otherwise a province of still water.
why.occupantsMotive: The reach is empty of fish. A portage crew works beside the reach. The crew charges by the hull. The crew holds a registered salvage claim on the reach. The interior tribes do not fish the reach.
why.pressures: Boats are lost at the Panther Race regularly. The portage crew profits from the losses. The people of Greenspring downstream receive the wreckage and the survivors. They resent both.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cleared channel would end the portage trade. It would also put laden craft no more than a day from Helstrom's approach. The escort service has costed that outcome and favours it.

preferences: water relation: the water IS the hazard
neighbours: forces every boat route to stop; a portage or a ferry always answers it

vibe.silhouette: The sound is heard from a long way upstream. White water follows the sound.
vibe.palette: Clear brown water breaks white over submerged root. Pale root-wood decking stands at the portage stand. Gold beads of sap hang on the underside of a spanning limb. Red flower colour has gone orange with age.
vibe.materials: Raw root-wood staging is driven at the portage landing. One abandoned rope is still tied off at the bank. A totem marks the crew's claimed stretch. The totem is unrenewed. Loose stone ballast is piled to steady the landing.
vibe.signatureFeature: Roots make the rapids, not rock. The whole reach is a lattice of submerged root.
vibe.condition: A licensed crew works the reach. The crew maintains the landing only well enough to keep the toll running.
vibe.approach: The Panther Race is heard from the last quiet bend.
vibe.senses: White water roars from a long bend upstream. Wet spray is cold even in the heat. The portage crew calls prices over the noise. Birds are absent from the loudest stretch.

places.whySiteWon: gorge in firm lowland (danger band 4), 192 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, route, landform.

playerPurpose.hook: The rapids are made of submerged root. They are not made of rock. A boat's crew must read the lattice before committing the boat. The portage crew charges by the hull.

loot.provenance: stripped from earlier travellers

places.name: The Turned Tree
sources: Lore:Hist (the eight Hist states); Lore:Lilmoth (the rogue Hist of 4E 48)

why.founding: The Turned Tree is a wild Hist with no tribe. It went wrong on its own. It stands in unkept ground.
why.siteAdvantages: The tree stands in a deep basin. No route passes it. It has no neighbours who would notice it for decades.
why.occupantsMotive: No tribe speaks for the tree. The nearest villages maintain a totem line and stay outside it. They re-cut the line outward each year as the ring widens.
why.pressures: The flowering ring is wider each year. The watchers of the counting tower have recorded the rate for three generations.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tribe that adopted the tree would most likely be destroyed. The Hist-less refuge has debated adopting it twice.

preferences: water relation: isolated water
neighbours: deliberately far from any living settlement

vibe.silhouette: The crown has grown wrong. Its limbs turn back on themselves. No chimes hang anywhere near it.
vibe.palette: Green shade doubles on still water. Gold beads hang under a turned limb. Algae covers every flat surface. One red flower is held still in the reflection.
vibe.materials: There is no built structure. The tree's own root serves as floor and wall. Crocodile skulls are set along the totem line. Trunks double back on themselves where the growth turned.
vibe.signatureFeature: Inside the flowering ring the trunks are doubled. The leaves face away from the light.
vibe.condition: The villages re-cut the totem line outward every year as the ring spreads.
vibe.mood: The tree feels wrong. The reason cannot be named.
vibe.approach: The birdsong stops about two hundred metres out.
vibe.senses: Birdsong stops well short of the flowering ring. Heat rises off ground that stays warm through cold nights. Bark ticks as it dries in still air. Leaves on every limb turn from the light.

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 483 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, region, danger.

playerPurpose.hook: The villages re-cut the totem line around the flowering ring outward each year. The animals inside the line do not leave.

loot.provenance: left by whoever came last

places.name: The Sleeper Under Ash
sources: Lore:Hist (the eight Hist states); Lore:Lilmoth (the rogue Hist of 4E 48)

why.founding: After the Duskfall, a Hist isolated itself from the collective. The isolated Hist sleeps. The Sleeper Under Ash grew from that Hist.
why.siteAdvantages: A burn scar never regrew around the tree. The tree stands alone in open ground.
why.occupantsMotive: No keeper tends the tree. Pilgrims come to sit here and do not come to speak. Sitting here is a recognised alternative for pilgrims who were refused audience at a hero grove.
why.pressures: The sap-tappers know that the tree cannot object to being tapped. The poacher camp works this tree in preference to any tree that has a tribe. The tree-minders know this but cannot prove it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Hist woke, three villages would have to renegotiate where they belong. Two of the villages pay the Agaceph grove for standing. Those two villages would no longer need that standing if the Hist woke.

preferences: water relation: isolated water
neighbours: deliberately far from any living settlement

vibe.silhouette: A great trunk stands under a mound of ash-grey moss. The trunk barely reads as a tree.
vibe.palette: Ash-grey moss lies thick over the trunk. The water is clear brown and pales to green beyond the scar. Old pale amber crusts the bark in thin lines. Red petals lie stuck flat to the wet wood.
vibe.materials: Root is shaped by permission only. One graft is allowed each generation. Withy binding is renewed over the older ties. None of the older ties is stripped away. Grass matting turns ash-grey where it has weathered longest. There is no built roof, only the open scar around the trunk.
vibe.signatureFeature: A living tree stands in a century of ash. The sky is open because the canopy burned away.
vibe.condition: The place is kept up by the effort of one pilgrim at a time. Otherwise it is untended.
vibe.mood: The place is still and open to the sky.
vibe.approach: The canopy stops at the burn scar. The ground beyond it is open to the sky.
vibe.senses: The open sky is unfamiliar after the closed canopy elsewhere. A chime frame has gone green and its cord has perished silent. A cold mineral smell comes off the mud at the edge of the scar. No horizon breaks the flat burned ground.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 682 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, region, danger.

playerPurpose.hook: A living tree stands alone in a century of ash. Pilgrims who were refused audience at a hero grove come and sit here.

loot.provenance: left by whoever came last

places.name: The Guide-Lights
sources: fauna-hazards dossier; module 55 (night light as a first-class world state)

why.founding: Travellers who follow the lights in this stretch of basin leave the route.
why.siteAdvantages: The basin lies between two safe rises. It lies on the line along which the guides walk.
why.occupantsMotive: The lights lie along a line between two safe rises. What the lights are is unknown. Whether they follow that line by design has not been tested.
why.pressures: Guides tell their clients that the lights are real and that the clients should ignore them. Clients follow the lights anyway. Survivors reach the far shelter and live on its stock.
why.wouldChangeIf: The guides price the crossing on the assumption that one client in twenty walks off the line. They make this assumption whatever the clients were told.

preferences: water relation: open standing water on a night route
neighbours: on a route people travel at night

vibe.silhouette: At night the lights themselves form the silhouette.
vibe.palette: Clear brown water is lit green from above. A lone red flower grows out of reach at the bank. No lantern light shows where lantern light is expected.
vibe.materials: Living root banks the basin on both sides. One cut step goes down to the water. The person who cut it regretted it. A blaze is cut into the last dry tree to mark the true line.
vibe.signatureFeature: The lights show the lantern rhythm of a guide, which is three short and one long. Every interior traveller is taught to trust that signal.
vibe.condition: The true line is kept clear only by the guides. They pass it on by word of mouth.
vibe.mood: The lights are a hazard that copies a signal.
vibe.approach: The correct signal shows in the wrong place.
vibe.senses: The air is still, then a light moves that no guide lit. The water shows its bottom clearly and looks deceptively shallow. No chime sounds anywhere along this stretch.

questHooks.opportunity: It can be proved in a quest that the lights copy the signal. The proof can be made before another party enters the basin.

places.whySiteWon: water narrows in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 167 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.

playerPurpose.hook: The lights repeat the lantern signal of the guides, which is three short and one long. They show it from the wrong place.

creatures.note: lure lights over the drop-off, where the water is deepest

loot.provenance: off travellers who followed the wrong lantern rhythm

places.name: The Made Ground

why.founding: The Hist grow Xal-Krona out of sap. Each making has a reason. The reason here was the Accord. The hollow was flooded with sap. The Hist made the Last Warden there. The remains in the basin are earlier attempts.
why.siteAdvantages: The basin is closed and is fed by deep roots. Sap collects there and does not drain away. Few places in the interior let a tree pool enough of its sap to make something of that size.
why.occupantsMotive: The basin is unoccupied. The Warden has not been here in an age. The Warden waits in the Lost City, as it was made to do. What remains here are the makings that came before it.
why.pressures: The basin still fills each wet season. What it grows now is smaller, wrong and short-lived. The Unbound Root have found the place and read it as a recipe.
why.wouldChangeIf: The making record here states what the Warden was made to test. If it is read first, it decides whether the Warden can be stood down or must be fought.

preferences: water relation: enclosed basin
neighbours: within reach of the Lost City approach
reached only through the Lost City: its deepest terrace, never a separate approach

places.traversalFallback: The fallback is the rim path around the basin. The rim path adds a day to the journey. The rim path stays out of the sap.

vibe.silhouette: A bowl of dead-still amber lies under a canopy that closes right over it. Pale ribs of something very large stand out of the surface at the low end.
vibe.palette: Amber pools waist-deep and is lit from below. The black-green canopy is sealed overhead. Red petals are scattered across the amber surface.
vibe.materials: Unbuilt sap-flooded root holds the shapes of failed makings. Bones are bleached pale where the sap has thinned around them. A ring of driven poles is set around the largest remains.
vibe.signatureFeature: Three skeletons lie in the sap at the shallow end. Each skeleton is larger than the last. Each skeleton is unfinished. At the deep end an empty impression the size of a house is still bare of growth.
vibe.condition: The basin has been undisturbed since the last making failed here.
vibe.approach: The way goes down the deep throat and out into a basin. The air in the basin is so sweet that it is hard to breathe.
vibe.senses: A chord is felt through the chest and is not heard. The sap hangs thick enough in the air to taste on the tongue. No insect sound is heard anywhere in the basin. A cold draught eases off as the basin opens out.

questHooks.opportunity: LOC warden.making_ground · EVIDENCE accord.making_record

localStateVariants.whatChanges: The making record in the basin is unread. The Warden is hostile to the visitor on meeting.

localStateVariants.when: This state applies after the making record is understood.
localStateVariants.whatChanges: The Warden can be stood down at the Lost City. What is growing in the basin stays dormant.

playerPurpose.hook: Three unfinished skeletons lie in the sap. Each is larger than the last. An empty impression the size of a house lies at the deep end.

loot.provenance: the Last Warden was made here; what is left in the sap is the working out

places.name: The Meeruth Station
sources: docs/quests/30-main-quest.md §24b.5 (player stronghold: reoccupied xanmeer OR abandoned river station)

why.founding: The Meeruth Station is an Imperial-era river station. It stands on the last navigable reach of the Helstrom approach. It was abandoned when the concession lapsed.
why.siteAdvantages: The station has a stone quay, a walled yard and a magazine. All of them stand on firm ground that the marsh cannot rot.
why.occupantsMotive: Squatters live here and leave when a claimant arrives. They have kept the magazine dry for twenty years.
why.pressures: The interior tribes and the Veiled Reed would both prefer that the station stayed unclaimed. Whoever holds a station on this reach controls the Helstrom approach outright.
why.wouldChangeIf: A claimant with standing could hold the station. That would put a fortified quay between Helstrom and the coast.

preferences: water relation: on the road, at water
neighbours: day-travel spacing along a road
water relation: a quay on the last navigable reach

vibe.silhouette: The station stands on the road and is visible from both approaches.
vibe.palette: Pale Imperial stone has gone grey with damp. The working quay is dark and slick at the waterline. Rust-red stains the hinges of the magazine door. Green shoots force through the old paving of the walled yard.
vibe.materials: The masonry shows three visible phases of Imperial work. Each phase is patched in a different hand. The magazine door is iron. Squatters have kept the magazine door oiled for twenty years. The quay stones are original and still level. The gate of the walled yard has stood open so long that its hinges have seized that way.
vibe.signatureFeature: A walled river yard has a working quay. The stonework shows three phases of building.
vibe.condition: Squatters keep the station dry and orderly. They leave the moment a claimant arrives.
vibe.approach: The magazine roof shows from the water before the quay does. The gate is open and has been open for a century.
vibe.senses: Wet heat comes off the river and does not lift at night. Gulls and river birds work the exposed mudbanks below the quay. The magazine door smells of iron each time it swings.

questHooks.opportunity: The station is a reserve player-stronghold site, `stronghold.site`. The primary stronghold is pirate-freeholds.rockpoint. The ruling for this is decision 0041 §12b.

places.reconciliation: This place is a candidate stronghold site. It is one site province-wide. It is reconciled against the xanmeer candidates of neighbouring agents before Part 3.

localStateVariants.whatChanges: The station is roofless and unlit. The road head is silted.

localStateVariants.when: This state applies if the station is claimed and held as a stronghold.
localStateVariants.whatChanges: The station is re-roofed and lit. The road head is cleared.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 106 m from the nearest route; no free 'river-mouth' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on nearPoint, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-repair'.

playerPurpose.hook: A walled river yard has a working quay and a dry magazine. The gate has been open for a century.

loot.provenance: an Imperial magazine the concession never emptied

places.name: Xal-Thuun
sources: Lore:Xanmeer (~20% inhabited; inhabited for their walls and still-working ancient defences)

why.founding: A tribe moved into the xanmeer of its ancestors during the Imperial century. The tribe never moved out.
why.siteAdvantages: Xal-Thuun has stone walls and working vakka mechanisms. These make it the strongest fortification in the interior.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe lives in a monument that it is meant solely to maintain. The tribe describes its residence as continuous tending.
why.pressures: Neighbouring tribes consider inhabiting the xanmeer to be close to the stone heresy. The mechanisms still kill people, mostly the young of the tribe. The deaths are recorded as falls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A mechanism failure would open the strongest position in the region. The vakka stones that drive the mechanisms are the largest cache in the interior.

preferences: water relation: raised; often moated by marsh
neighbours: dominates its immediate district

notableNpcSlots.role: The kaal who holds the terraces
The keeper who knows which mechanisms still work

vibe.silhouette: The silhouette is terraced monumental massing. Smoke and washing lie on the terraces.
vibe.palette: The terraces are green-grey and are kept deliberately clear of growth. Amber lamplight shows in the stair mouths after dark. A single red flower grows on the lone tree that stands inside the walls. The stone underfoot is black and wet.
vibe.materials: The tribe maintains the xanmeer stone and does not replace it. Neighbouring tribes object to this. Trained root binds the newer additions to the old. Withy and flint-vine lash the hoardings in place. Working vakka mechanisms are set into the terrace walls.
vibe.signatureFeature: Working xanmeer traps guard a doorway. Laundry hangs across the doorway.
vibe.condition: The tribe lives in the fort and maintains it daily. The tribe leaves its traps running. The traps are occasionally fatal.
vibe.approach: The terraces break the canopy. The smoke comes out of the terraces.
vibe.senses: The stone treads ring underfoot at every terrace. Laundry snaps in the wind across a trap doorway. A mechanism resets somewhere below with a distant clunk. Cooking smoke drifts out across the walls.

places.whySiteWon: summit in firm lowland (danger band 5), 98 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, route.

playerPurpose.hook: Working xanmeer traps guard a doorway with laundry hung across it. The tribe living inside describes that as maintenance.

loot.provenance: a fort that has never been taken
